sentences.zh: 左懋第祁彪佳

translations.literal: Zuo Maodi, Qi Biaojia
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Maodi, Qi Biaojia

sentences.zh: 天啟初，出督畿輔屯田，言：「天津、靜海、興濟間，沃野萬頃，可墾為田。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he went out to supervise military colony lands in the capital region and memorialized: "Between Tianjin, Jinghai, and Xingji lies ten thousand qing of fertile land that could be opened for cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was sent to oversee military colony lands around the capital and wrote: "Between Tianjin, Jinghai, and Xingji there is ten thousand qing of rich soil that could be brought under the plow.

sentences.zh: 近同知盧觀象墾田三千余畝，其溝洫廬舍之制，種植疏浚之方，犁然具備，可仿而行。

translations.literal: Recently the vice prefect Lu Guanxiang opened more than three thousand mu of fields; his systems for ditches, dwellings, planting, and dredging were fully in place and clear, and could be imitated and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago Vice Prefect Lu Guanxiang had reclaimed more than three thousand mu; his layout of canals, housing, planting, and dredging was already complete and could serve as a model.

sentences.zh: 」因列上官種、佃種、民種、軍種、屯種五法。

translations.literal: " He then listed five methods: official planting, tenant planting, civilian planting, military planting, and colony planting.
translations.idiomatic: " He went on to set out five methods—planting by officials, by tenants, by civilians, by soldiers, and by colony troops.

sentences.zh: 又言：「廣寧失守，遼人轉徙入關者不下百萬。

translations.literal: He also said: "When Guangning fell, no fewer than a million people from Liaodong who relocated into the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "After Guangning was lost, at least a million Liaodong refugees moved inside the passes.

sentences.zh: 宜招集津門，以無家之眾，墾不耕之田便。

translations.literal: They should be gathered at Jingmen so that those without homes might conveniently open fields that were not being cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: They ought to be assembled at Tianjin so homeless multitudes could conveniently work land that lay fallow.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An imperial decree approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 嘗疏薦趙南星，劾馮銓，銓大恨。

translations.literal: He once memorialized recommending Zhao Nanxing and impeaching Feng Quan; Quan came to hate him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: He once recommended Zhao Nanxing and impeached Feng Quan, who thereafter hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，慎言假歸，銓屬曹欽程論劾，誣盜曹縣庫銀三千，遂下撫按征臟，編戍肅州。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, Shenyan took leave to return home; Quan had Cao Qincheng draft an impeachment, falsely accusing him of stealing three thousand taels of silver from the Cao County treasury; he was then sent down to the grand coordinator and regional inspector to collect the booty, and was banished to garrison duty at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year Shenyan went home on leave; Quan had Cao Qincheng impeach him, falsely claiming he had embezzled three thousand taels from the Cao County treasury. The case was sent to the provincial authorities to recover the sum, and he was banished to military service at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 十七年三月，京師陷。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year, the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventeenth year the capital fell to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 五月，福王即位南京，命慎言理部事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Prince of Fu ascended the throne at Nanjing and ordered Shenyan to handle ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Prince of Fu took the throne at Nanjing and put Shenyan in charge of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 上中興十議：曰節鎮，曰親藩，曰開屯，曰叛逆，曰偽命，曰褒恤，曰功賞，曰起廢，曰懲貪，曰漕稅。

translations.literal: He submitted Ten Discussions for Restoration: on curtailing regional commanders, on imperial clansmen, on opening military colonies, on rebels, on false commands, on rewards and posthumous honors, on merit awards, on restoring the dismissed, on punishing corruption, and on grain transport taxes.
translations.idiomatic: He presented Ten Proposals for Restoration—on curbing regional commanders, on imperial clans, on opening colony lands, on rebels, on forged orders, on honors for the dead, on rewarding merit, on recalling the dismissed, on punishing graft, and on grain transport and taxation.

sentences.zh: 皆嘉納。

translations.literal: All were praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court welcomed them all.

sentences.zh: 時大起廢籍，慎言薦吳甡、鄭三俊。

translations.literal: At the time dismissed officials were being widely recalled; Shenyan recommended Wu Shen and Zheng Sanjun.
translations.idiomatic: Officials long out of office were being recalled in large numbers; Shenyan nominated Wu Shen and Zheng Sanjun.

sentences.zh: 命甡陛見，三俊不許，大學士高弘圖所擬也。

translations.literal: Wu Shen was ordered to audience at court; Zheng Sanjun was not permitted—this was as Grand Secretary Gao Hongtu had proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shen was summoned to audience; Zheng Sanjun was denied—at the proposal of Grand Secretary Gao Hongtu.

sentences.zh: 勛臣劉孔昭，趙之龍等一日朝罷，群詬於廷，指慎言及甡為奸邪，叱咤徹殿陛。

translations.literal: One day after court adjourned, meritorious nobles Liu Kongzhao, Zhao Zhilong, and others gathered in the hall berating as treacherous Shenyan and Wu Shen, shouting all the way to the palace steps.
translations.idiomatic: One day after court, meritorious nobles Liu Kongzhao, Zhao Zhilong, and others mobbed the hall, calling Shenyan and Wu Shen traitors and roaring all the way to the palace steps.

sentences.zh: 給事中羅萬象言：「慎言平生具在，甡素有清望，安得指為奸邪？

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Luo Wanxiang said: "Shenyan's whole life is on record; Wu Shen has long enjoyed a reputation for integrity—how can they be called treacherous?
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Luo Wanxiang said: "Shenyan's whole career is on record, and Wu Shen has long been known for integrity—how can they be called traitors?

sentences.zh: 」孔昭等伏地痛哭，謂慎言舉用文臣，不及武臣，囂爭不已。

translations.literal: " Kongzhao and the others prostrated themselves weeping, saying Shenyan in his appointments favored civil officials and not military officers, and clamored without cease.
translations.idiomatic: " Kongzhao and his party threw themselves down weeping, claiming Shenyan promoted civil men and neglected military officers, and would not stop shouting.

sentences.zh: 又疏劾慎言，極詆三俊。

translations.literal: They again memorialized impeaching Shenyan and bitterly reviling Sanjun.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized again to impeach Shenyan and savaged Sanjun.

sentences.zh: 且謂：：「慎言當迎立時，阻難懷二心。

translations.literal: They also said: "When Shenyan should have welcomed the enthronement, he obstructed and harbored divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: They also charged that when the heir was to be welcomed, Shenyan had obstructed the matter and harbored divided loyalties.

sentences.zh: 乞寢牲陛見命，且議慎言欺蔽罪。

translations.literal: They asked that Wu Shen's command to audience be suspended and that Shenyan's crime of deception be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that Wu Shen's summons to audience be set aside and that Shenyan's deceit of the throne be investigated.

sentences.zh: 」慎言疏辨，因乞休。

translations.literal: " Shenyan memorialized in rebuttal and asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: " Shenyan answered in a memorial and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 萬象又言：「首膺封爵者，四鎮也。

translations.literal: Wanxiang also said: "Those first granted enfeoffment were the four regional commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Wanxiang added: "The first to receive enfeoffment were the four regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 新改京營，又加二鎮銜，何嘗不用武。

translations.literal: When the capital garrison was reorganized, two more commanders' titles were added—when were military men not employed?
translations.idiomatic: The capital garrison was just reorganized and two more commanders' titles added—when were military men not used?

sentences.zh: 年來封疆之法，先帝多寬武臣，武臣報先帝者安在？

translations.literal: In recent years the policy toward the borders—how much the late emperor indulged military men—where are the military men who repaid the late emperor?
translations.idiomatic: For years frontier policy indulged military men—where are the soldiers who repaid the late emperor?

sentences.zh: 祖制以票擬歸閣臣，參駁歸言官，不聞委勛臣以糾劾也。

translations.literal: By ancestral institution, drafting with vermilion notes belonged to Grand Secretaries and rebuttal to supervising officials; one never heard of entrusting meritorious nobles with impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: By ancestral usage memorial drafts went to Grand Secretaries and rebuttal to remonstrance officials; meritorious nobles were never entrusted with impeachment.

sentences.zh: 使勛臣得兼糾劾，文臣可勝逐哉！

translations.literal: If meritorious nobles could also impeach, could civil officials survive being driven out!
translations.idiomatic: If nobles of merit could also impeach, what civil minister could keep his post!

sentences.zh: 」史可法奏：「慎言疏薦無不當。

translations.literal: " Shi Kefa memorialized: "None of Shenyan's recommendations in his memorial was inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi Kefa wrote: "Every man Shenyan recommended was fit for his post.

sentences.zh: 諸臣痛哭喧呼，滅絕法紀，恐驕弁悍卒益輕朝廷。

translations.literal: The various officials wept and clamored, extinguishing law and discipline; I fear arrogant officers and fierce soldiers will all the more hold the court in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: These men wept and shouted, trampling law and order; I fear arrogant commanders and unruly troops will hold the court in still greater contempt.

sentences.zh: 」御史王孫蕃言：「用人，吏部職掌。

translations.literal: " The investigating censor Wang Sunfan said: "Appointing men is the Ministry of Personnel's duty.
translations.idiomatic: " Censor Wang Sunfan said: "Appointments are the Ministry of Personnel's business.

sentences.zh: 奈何廷辱冢宰。

translations.literal: How can one insult the chief minister in court?
translations.idiomatic: How can the chief minister be humiliated in open court?

sentences.zh: 」弘圖等亦以不能戢和文武，各疏乞休，不允。

translations.literal: " Hongtu and others also, being unable to restrain civil and military harmony, each memorialized asking to retire, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongtu and others, unable to reconcile civil and military factions, each asked to resign; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 甡既不出，慎言乞休得請，加太子太保，蔭一子。

translations.literal: Since Wu Shen did not come out, Shenyan's request to retire was granted; he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and one son ennobled.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shen never took office; Shenyan's resignation was granted, with the added title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and hereditary privilege for one son.

sentences.zh: 山西盡陷於賊，慎言無家可歸，流寓蕪湖、宣城間。

translations.literal: Shanxi was entirely lost to bandits; Shenyan had no home to return to and drifted between Wuhu and Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi fell entirely to rebels; Shenyan had no home to return to and wandered between Wuhu and Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 國亡後，疽發於背，戒勿藥，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: After the state's fall, a carbuncle broke out on his back; he warned against medicine and died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynasty collapsed an abscess broke out on his back; he forbade medicine and died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 慎言少喪二親，鞠於祖母。

translations.literal: In his youth Shenyan lost both parents and was raised by his grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyan lost both parents in childhood and was raised by his grandmother.

sentences.zh: 及為御史，訃聞，引義乞歸，執喪三年以報。

translations.literal: When he became an investigating censor and news of mourning arrived, he cited propriety to ask leave and observed mourning for three years in return.
translations.idiomatic: When he became a censor and word of his grandmother's death arrived, he cited propriety to ask leave and observed three years of mourning in her stead.

sentences.zh: 子履旋，舉崇禎十五年鄉試。

translations.literal: His son Lüxuan passed the provincial examination in the fifteenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lüxuan passed the provincial examination in the fifteenth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 賊陷陽城，投崖死。

translations.literal: When bandits took Yangcheng, he threw himself from a cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels seized Yangcheng he threw himself from a cliff and died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈御史。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, he was posthumously granted investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court he was posthumously made investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 徐石麒，字寶摩，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Xu Shiqi, styled Baomo, was a native of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shiqi, courtesy name Baomo, was from Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 授工部營繕主事，筦節慎庫。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Works for construction and managed the Jieshen treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works' construction bureau and oversaw the Jieshen treasury.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢兼領惜薪司，所需悉從庫發，石麒輒持故事格之。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian concurrently headed the Fuelwood Office; everything required was drawn from the treasury, and Shiqi repeatedly held to precedent to block it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian also ran the Fuelwood Office and drew every need from the treasury; Shiqi repeatedly blocked him on precedent.

sentences.zh: 其黨噪於庭，不為動。

translations.literal: His faction clamored in the courtyard but he was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian's men raised a clamor in the courtyard; he did not budge.

sentences.zh: 御史黃尊素坐忤忠賢下詔獄，石麒為盡力。

translations.literal: The investigating censor Huang Zunsu, having offended Zhongxian, was sent to the imperial prison; Shiqi exerted himself to the utmost on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Huang Zunsu offended Zhongxian and was sent to the imperial prison; Shiqi did all he could for him.

sentences.zh: 忠賢怒，執新城侯王升子下獄，令誣賄石麒，捕系其家人，勒完臟而削其籍。

translations.literal: Zhongxian in anger had the son of the Marquis of Xincheng, Wang Sheng, seized and put in prison, ordering him to falsely accuse Shiqi of taking bribes; Shiqi's family were arrested, compelled to pay the full penalty, and his name was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian in rage had the Marquis of Xincheng's son Wang Sheng imprisoned and made to accuse Shiqi of bribery; Shiqi's family were seized, forced to pay the full penalty, and his name was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，起南京禮部主事，就遷考功郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he was recalled as principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites and soon promoted to director in the Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongzhen he was recalled as a principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites and soon promoted to director in the Bureau of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 八年佐尚書鄭三俊京察，澄汰至公。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he assisted Minister Zheng Sanjun in the capital's annual review, clarifying and eliminating with utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he assisted Minister Zheng Sanjun in the capital review, purging the roster with scrupulous fairness.

sentences.zh: 歷尚寶卿、應天府丞。

translations.literal: He passed through Chamberlain for Imperial Insignia and vice prefect of Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chamberlain of the imperial insignia and as vice prefect of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 十一年春入賀。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year he entered the capital to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year he went to the capital to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 三俊時為刑部尚書，議侯恂獄不中，得罪。

translations.literal: Sanjun was then Minister of Justice; his ruling in the Hou Xun case was deemed incorrect and he was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Sanjun was then Minister of Justice; his judgment in the Hou Xun case was found wanting and he was punished.

sentences.zh: 石麒疏救，釋之。

translations.literal: Shiqi memorialized in rescue and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi memorialized in his defense and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 石麒官南京十余年，至是始入為左通政，累遷光祿卿、通政使。

translations.literal: Shiqi had served more than ten years at Nanjing; only now did he enter the capital as left vice commissioner of communications and was successively promoted chamberlain of imperial sacrificial wine and commissioner of communications.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi had served at Nanjing for more than ten years; only now did he enter the capital as left vice commissioner of communications, rising in time to chamberlain of imperial sacrificial wine and commissioner of communications.

sentences.zh: 十五年擢刑部右侍郎，讞吏部尚書李日宣等獄。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted vice minister of justice on the right and judged cases of Minister of Personnel Li Rixuan and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made vice minister of justice on the right and sentenced Minister of Personnel Li Rixuan and others.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「枚卜大典，日宣稱詡徇私。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The great ceremony of selecting the Grand Secretariat—Rixuan praised and showed favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "In the great lot-drawing for Grand Secretaries, Rixuan praised men and showed favoritism.

sentences.zh: 」石麒予輕比，貶二秩。

translations.literal: " Shiqi gave a lighter analogy and was demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: " Shiqi gave a lighter sentence and was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 先是，會推閣臣，日宣一再推，因及副都御史房可壯、工部右侍郎宋玫、大理寺卿張三謨，石麒與焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the joint recommendation for Grand Secretary, Rixuan had repeatedly pushed forward, bringing in also vice censor-in-chief Fang Kezhuang, vice minister of works Song Mei, and chief justice Zhang Sanmo—Shiqi was among them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the joint nomination for Grand Secretary, Rixuan had pushed repeatedly, bringing in Vice Censor-in-Chief Fang Kezhuang, Vice Minister of Works Song Mei, and Chief Justice Zhang Sanmo—Shiqi among them.

sentences.zh: 召對便殿，石麒獨不赴。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience in the side hall, Shiqi alone did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned to audience in the side hall, Shiqi alone did not go.

sentences.zh: 及是帝怒，戍日宣及吏科都給事中章正宸、河南道御史張煊，奪可壯、玫、三謨及讞獄左侍郎惠世揚官。

translations.literal: At this the emperor in anger banished Rixuan and Chief Supervising Secretary of the Department of Personnel Zhang Zhengkai and Henan investigating censor Zhang Xuan, and stripped Kezhuang, Mei, Sanmo, and left vice minister of justice who judged the case, Hui Shiyang, of their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor in anger banished Rixuan, Chief Supervising Secretary Zhang Zhengkai, and Henan investigating censor Zhang Xuan, and stripped Kezhuang, Mei, Sanmo, and left vice minister Hui Shiyang, who had judged the case, of office.

sentences.zh: 石麒代世揚掌部事，旋進左。

translations.literal: Shiqi replaced Shiyang to head the ministry and soon advanced to the left.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi replaced Shiyang as acting head of the ministry and soon advanced to the left vice ministership.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝以威刑馭下，法官引律，大抵深文附會，予重比。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor governed his subordinates with severe punishments; judicial officials citing statutes mostly twisted the text to fit and gave heavy penalties.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor ruled his officials through harsh punishments; judges citing the code mostly twisted the text and imposed heavy sentences.

sentences.zh: 石麒奉命清獄，推明律意，校正今斷獄之不合於律者十余章，先以白同官。

translations.literal: Shiqi received orders to clear the prisons, expounded the intent of the statutes, and corrected more than ten articles in current adjudication that did not accord with the law, first informing his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi was ordered to review the prisons, expounded the intent of the statutes, and corrected more than ten articles in current sentencing that did not match the code, informing his colleagues first.

sentences.zh: 以次審理十三司囚，多寬減。

translations.literal: He then in order tried prisoners of the thirteen departments, many reduced or lightened.
translations.idiomatic: He then tried prisoners of the thirteen departments in turn, lightening many sentences.

sentences.zh: 然廉公，一時大法赫然，無敢幸免者。

translations.literal: Yet he was upright and fair; for a time the great law was sternly manifest and none dared escape.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was incorrupt and fair; for a time the law stood stern and none dared hope to escape it.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書陳新甲下獄，朝士多營救。

translations.literal: Minister of War Chen Xin jia was put in prison; court scholars mostly interceded.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Chen Xin jia was imprisoned; many at court pleaded for him.

sentences.zh: 石麒持之曰：「人臣無境外交。

translations.literal: Shiqi held firm, saying: "As ministers there is no diplomacy beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi held firm: "Ministers may not conduct diplomacy beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 未有身在朝廷，不告君父而專擅便宜者。

translations.literal: Never has one been at court, not informing ruler and father, yet acting on his own convenience.
translations.idiomatic: No one at court may act on his own authority without informing his sovereign and father.

sentences.zh: 新甲私款辱國，當失陷城寨律，斬。

translations.literal: Xin jia's private overtures shamed the state; he should be judged under the statute for losing frontier fortresses and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Xin jia's secret dealings shamed the state; he should be judged under the statute for losing frontier fortresses and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「未中，可覆擬。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Not quite right; you may revise the finding.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "That does not fit; revise the sentence.

sentences.zh: 」乃論新甲陷邊城四，陷腹城七十二，陷親藩七，從來未有之奇禍。

translations.literal: " They then judged Xin jia as having lost four frontier cities, seventy-two interior cities, and seven imperial clansmen's domains—an unprecedented extraordinary calamity.
translations.idiomatic: " They then judged that Xin jia had lost four frontier cities, seventy-two interior cities, and seven imperial fiefs—an unprecedented calamity.

sentences.zh: 當臨敵缺乏，不依期進兵策應，因而失誤軍機者斬。

translations.literal: When facing the enemy lacking supplies, failing to advance troops on schedule in support—such as disrupts military opportunity—is capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever, facing the enemy short of supplies, fails to advance troops on schedule in support and thereby loses the military opportunity, is to be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 奏上，新甲棄市，新甲黨皆大恨。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, Xin jia was executed in the marketplace; Xin jia's faction all hated deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial went up, Xin jia was executed in the marketplace; his faction hated Shiqi bitterly.

sentences.zh: 石麒尋擢本部尚書。

translations.literal: Shiqi was soon promoted minister of the same ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi was soon made minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 中官王裕民坐劉元斌黨，元斌縱軍淫掠，伏誅，裕民以欺隱不舉下獄。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Yumin was implicated in Liu Yuanbin's faction; Yuanbin let his troops ravage and loot, was executed, and Yumin for concealing and not reporting was put in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Wang Yumin was implicated with Liu Yuanbin, who had let his troops plunder and was executed; Yumin was imprisoned for concealing the crime and failing to report it.

sentences.zh: 帝欲殺之，初令三法司同鞫，後專付刑部，石麒議戍煙瘴。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to kill him; at first he ordered the Three Departments to try jointly, then entrusted it solely to the Ministry of Justice; Shiqi recommended banishment to miasmal frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to kill him; at first he ordered the Three Departments to try the case jointly, then gave it solely to the Ministry of Justice; Shiqi recommended exile to the miasmal frontier.

sentences.zh: 奏成，署院寺名以進。

translations.literal: When the memorial was complete, he signed the names of the court and ministry to present it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was finished he signed the names of the court and ministry and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 帝怒其失出，召詰都御史劉宗周，對曰：「此獄非臣讞。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry at the lenient outcome and summoned and questioned Censor-in-chief Liu Zongzhou, who replied: "This case was not my judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry at the lenient sentence and summoned Censor-in-Chief Liu Zongzhou, who replied: "This case was not judged by me.

sentences.zh: 」徐曰：「臣雖不與聞，然閱讞同，已曲盡情事。

translations.literal: " After a pause he said: "Though I did not hear of it, in reading the joint judgment I have already fully exhausted the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: " After a pause he said: "Though I did not take part, in reading the joint judgment I see the facts are fully set out.

sentences.zh: 刑官所執者法耳。

translations.literal: What criminal officials uphold is the law alone.
translations.idiomatic: Judges uphold only the law.

sentences.zh: 法如是止，石麒非私裕民也。

translations.literal: The law stops here; Shiqi did not show private favor to Yumin.
translations.idiomatic: The law stops there; Shiqi did not favor Yumin out of private regard.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此奴欺罔實甚，卿等焉知？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "This slave's deception was very great—how would you know?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "This slave's deceit was grave—how would you know?

sentences.zh: 」令石麒改讞詞，棄之市。

translations.literal: " He ordered Shiqi to revise the finding; Yumin was abandoned in the market.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Shiqi to revise the sentence; Yumin was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 無何，宗周以救姜埰，熊開元獲嚴譴，僉都御史金光辰救之，奪職。

translations.literal: Before long Zongzhou for rescuing Jiang Kai and Xiong Kaiyuan received severe punishment; vice censor-in-chief Jin Guangchen for rescuing him was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zongzhou was severely punished for pleading for Jiang Kai and Xiong Kaiyuan; Vice Censor-in-Chief Jin Guangchen, who had pleaded for Zongzhou, was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 石麒再疏留，不納。

translations.literal: Shiqi again memorialized to retain them; this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi memorialized again to keep them in office; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 玘、開元既下詔獄，移刑部定罪。

translations.literal: Kai and Kaiyuan having been sent to the imperial prison, the case was transferred to the Ministry of Justice for sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: Kai and Kaiyuan having been sent to the imperial prison, the case was transferred to the Ministry of Justice for sentencing.

sentences.zh: 石麒據原詞擬開元贖徒，埰謫戍，不復鞫訊。

translations.literal: Shiqi according to the original accusation proposed Kaiyuan ransom labor, Kai banished to garrison, without further interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi, going by the original charges, proposed ransom labor for Kaiyuan and banishment for Kai, without further interrogation.

sentences.zh: 帝責對狀，石麒援故事對。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered face-to-face reply; Shiqi cited precedent in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to answer in person; Shiqi cited precedent.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，除司官三人名，石麒落職閑住。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, removed three officials' names from the rolls, and Shiqi was dismissed and left idle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, struck three officials from the rolls, and Shiqi was dismissed to idle residence.

sentences.zh: 福王監國，召拜右都御史，未任，改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu supervised the state, he was summoned as right censor-in-chief; before taking office he was changed to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu supervised the state, Shiqi was summoned as right censor-in-chief; before he took office he was made Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 奏陳省庶官、慎破格、行久任、重名器、嚴起廢、明保舉、交堂廉七事。

translations.literal: He memorialized seven items: reducing superfluous offices, caution in irregular promotions, long tenure, valuing titles, strict restoration of the dismissed, clear recommendations, and mixing offices for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on seven matters: cutting redundant posts, caution in irregular promotions, long tenure, respect for titles, strict standards for recalling the dismissed, clarity in recommendations, and rotating offices to preserve integrity.

sentences.zh: 時方考選，與都御史劉宗周矢公甄別，以年例出御史黃耳鼎、給事中陸朗於外。

translations.literal: Selection was then under review; with Censor-in-chief Liu Zongzhou he vowed impartial distinction, and by seniority sent investigating censor Huang Erding and supervising secretary Lu Lang outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Selection was then under way; with Censor-in-Chief Liu Zongzhou he pledged impartial judgment and, by seniority, sent investigating censor Huang Erding and supervising secretary Lu Lang out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 朗賄奄人得留用，石麒發其罪。

translations.literal: Lang bribed eunuchs to be retained; Shiqi exposed his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Lang bribed eunuchs to stay in office; Shiqi exposed his crime.

sentences.zh: 朗恚，詆石麒，石麒稱疾乞休。

translations.literal: Lang in rage reviled Shiqi; Shiqi claimed illness and asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Lang in fury slandered Shiqi; Shiqi pleaded illness and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 耳鼎亦兩疏劾石麒，並言其枉殺陳新甲。

translations.literal: Erding also twice memorialized impeaching Shiqi, and also said he had wrongly killed Chen Xin jia.
translations.idiomatic: Erding too memorialized twice to impeach Shiqi, charging that he had unjustly executed Chen Xin jia.

sentences.zh: 石麒疏辯，求去益力。

translations.literal: Shiqi memorialized in rebuttal and asked to leave with greater force.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi answered in a memorial and pressed all the harder to resign.

sentences.zh: 馬士英擬嚴旨，福王不許，命馳驛歸。

translations.literal: Ma Shiying drafted a severe edict; the Prince of Fu did not permit it and ordered him to return home by express relay.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiying drafted a harsh edict; the Prince of Fu refused and ordered Shiqi home by express relay.

sentences.zh: 石麒剛方清介，扼於權奸，悒悒不得誌。

translations.literal: Shiqi was upright, stern, and pure; constrained by powerful traitors, he was depressed and unable to fulfill his aims.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi was upright and incorruptible, but hemmed in by powerful traitors and could not achieve what he intended.

sentences.zh: 士英挾定策功，將圖封，石麒議格之。

translations.literal: Shiying relied on his merit in settling the succession and was about to seek enfeoffment; Shiqi's proposal blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying, trading on his role in securing the succession, sought enfeoffment; Shiqi's proposal blocked it.

sentences.zh: 中官田成輩納賄請囑，石麒悉拒不應。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Tian Cheng and his ilk offered bribes to request favors; Shiqi entirely refused and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs such as Tian Cheng offered bribes to solicit favors; Shiqi refused them all.

sentences.zh: 由是中外皆怨，構之去。

translations.literal: Because of this court and countryside alike resented him and contrived his removal.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside alike resented him and contrived his removal.

sentences.zh: 去後以登極恩，加太子太保。

translations.literal: After he left, by grace of the enthronement he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After he left he was given the added title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent as part of the enthronement favors.

sentences.zh: 明年，南都亡。

translations.literal: The next year, the Southern Capital perished.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Southern Capital fell.

sentences.zh: 石麒時居郡城外，城將破，石麒曰：「吾大臣也，城亡與亡！

translations.literal: Shiqi was then living outside the prefectural city; as the city was about to fall, Shiqi said: "I am a great minister—the city perishes and I perish with it!
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi was then living outside the city walls; as the city was about to fall he said: "I am a chief minister—when the city falls, I fall with it!

sentences.zh: 」復入居城中，以閏月二十六日朝服自縊死，年六十有八。

translations.literal: " He again entered to live within the city and on the twenty-sixth day of the intercalary month hanged himself in court dress, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: " He went back inside the city and on the twenty-sixth day of the intercalary month hanged himself in court dress at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 解學龍，字石帆，揚州興化人。

translations.literal: Jie Xuelong, styled Shifan, was a native of Xinghua in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Xuelong, courtesy name Shifan, was from Xinghua in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the forty-first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-first year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 歷金華、東昌二府推官。

translations.literal: He passed through posts as judicial assistant in the prefectures of Jinhua and Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial assistant in Jinhua and Dongchang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，擢刑科給事中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was promoted supervising secretary in the Department of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi he was made supervising secretary in the Department of Justice.

sentences.zh: 遼東難民多渡海聚登州，招練副使劉國縉請帑金十萬振之，多所幹沒。

translations.literal: Many refugees from Liaodong crossed the sea and gathered at Dengzhou; the vice commissioner for recruitment and training Liu Guojin requested one hundred thousand taels from the treasury to relieve them, much of which was embezzled.
translations.idiomatic: Many Liaodong refugees crossed the sea and gathered at Dengzhou; Vice Commissioner Liu Guojin asked for one hundred thousand taels from the treasury to relieve them, and much of it was embezzled.

sentences.zh: 學龍三疏發其弊，國縉遂獲譴。

translations.literal: Xuelong three times memorialized exposing the abuses, and Guojin then received punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Xuelong exposed the abuses in three memorials, and Guojin was punished.

sentences.zh: 王紀忤魏忠賢削籍，學龍言：「紀亮節弘猷，召置廊廟，必能表正百僚，裁決大務。

translations.literal: Wang Ji offended Wei Zhongxian and was struck from the rolls; Xuelong said: "Ji has bright integrity and broad plans; summoned to the hall and temple, he will surely be able to set an example for the hundred officials and decide great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji offended Wei Zhongxian and was struck from the rolls; Xuelong wrote: "Ji has bright integrity and broad vision; if recalled to court he could set an example for the bureaucracy and decide great affairs.

sentences.zh: 」失忠賢意，不報。

translations.literal: " This displeased Zhongxian and received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: " This displeased Zhongxian and received no response.

sentences.zh: 已，劾川、貴舊總督張我續貪淫漏網，新總督楊述中縮朒卸責，帝不罪。

translations.literal: Later he impeached the former Sichuan-Guizhou governor Zhang Woxu for greed and debauchery escaping the net, and the new governor Yang Shuzhong for shrinking and shirking responsibility; the emperor did not punish them.
translations.idiomatic: He later impeached the former Sichuan-Guizhou governor Zhang Woxu for corruption and debauchery that had gone unpunished, and the new governor Yang Shuzhong for shirking responsibility; the emperor took no action.

sentences.zh: 學龍通曉政務。

translations.literal: Xuelong was thoroughly versed in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xuelong was thoroughly versed in government affairs.

sentences.zh: 上言：

translations.literal: He memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized:

sentences.zh: 遼左額兵舊九萬四千有奇，幾餉四十余萬。

translations.literal: The quota troops in eastern Liaodong formerly numbered more than ninety-four thousand odd, with rations of nearly four hundred thousand odd.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Liaodong once had a quota of more than ninety-four thousand troops, with rations of nearly four hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 今關上兵止十余萬，月餉乃二十二萬。

translations.literal: Now troops at the passes number only a little more than one hundred thousand, yet monthly rations are two hundred twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Today there are barely one hundred thousand troops at the passes, yet monthly pay runs to two hundred twenty thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 遼兵盡潰，關門宜募新兵。

translations.literal: Liaodong troops have all scattered; the passes should recruit new soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong armies have collapsed; the passes should recruit fresh troops.

sentences.zh: 薊鎮舊有額兵，乃亦給厚糈召募。

translations.literal: Jizhou garrison had quota troops of old, yet thick rations were also given to recruit.
translations.idiomatic: The Jizhou garrison already had quota troops, yet rich pay was also offered to recruit more.

sentences.zh: 舊兵以其餉厚，悉竄入新營，而舊額又如故，漏卮可勝言。

translations.literal: Old soldiers because their rations were thick all slipped into new camps, while the old quotas remained as before—the leaking vessel can hardly be described.
translations.idiomatic: Old soldiers, drawn by the higher pay, all slipped into the new camps while the old quotas remained on the books—the waste is beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 國初，文職五千四百有奇，武職二萬八千有奇。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state, civil posts numbered more than five thousand four hundred odd, military posts more than twenty-eight thousand odd.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding there were more than five thousand four hundred civil posts and more than twenty-eight thousand military posts.

sentences.zh: 神祖時，文增至一萬六千余，武增至八萬二千余矣。

translations.literal: In the time of the Divine Ancestor, civil posts increased to more than sixteen thousand, military to more than eighty-two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By the reign of the Shenzong Emperor civil posts had risen to more than sixteen thousand and military posts to more than eighty-two thousand.

sentences.zh: 今不知又增幾倍。

translations.literal: Now one does not know by how many times more they have increased.
translations.idiomatic: Today they have surely multiplied again beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 誠度冗者汰之，歲可得餉數十萬。

translations.literal: If one truly estimated the redundant and eliminated them, each year one could obtain rations of several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: If redundant posts were truly identified and cut, several hundred thousand taels in pay could be saved each year.

sentences.zh: 裁冗吏，核曠卒，俾衛所應襲子弟襲職而不給俸，又可得數十萬。

translations.literal: Cut redundant clerks, verify vacant soldiers, and have guard and battalion heirs who should inherit posts inherit office without salary—one could again obtain several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Cut redundant clerks, verify vacant soldiers, and let guard and battalion heirs inherit posts without pay—another several hundred thousand could be saved.

sentences.zh: 京邊米一石，民輸則非一石也。

translations.literal: For one shi of grain at the capital frontiers, what the people deliver is not one shi.
translations.idiomatic: For every shi of grain at the capital frontiers, what the people actually deliver is not one shi.

sentences.zh: 以民之費與國之收衷之，國之一，民之三。

translations.literal: Comparing the people's cost with the state's receipt, the state gets one, the people three.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh the people's cost against the state's receipt: the state gets one part, the people three.

sentences.zh: 關餉一斛銀四錢，以易錢則好米值錢百，惡米止三四十錢，又其下腐臭不可食。

translations.literal: Frontier rations were four qian of silver per hu; exchanged for cash, good rice was worth one hundred cash, bad rice only thirty or forty, and below that rotten and stinking, inedible.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier grain allowance was four qian of silver per hu; exchanged for cash, good rice fetched one hundred cash, poor rice only thirty or forty, and below that it was rotten and inedible.

sentences.zh: 以國之費與兵之食衷之，兵之一，國之三。

translations.literal: Comparing the state's cost with what the soldiers eat, the soldiers get one, the state three.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh the state's cost against what the soldiers eat: the soldiers get one part, the state three.

sentences.zh: 總計之，民費其六，而兵食其一。

translations.literal: In total, the people pay six parts and the soldiers eat one.
translations.idiomatic: In all, the people pay six parts and the soldiers receive one.

sentences.zh: 況小民作奸欺漕卒，漕卒欺官司，官司欺天子，展轉相欺，米已化為糠比沙土；

translations.literal: Moreover common people commit fraud to deceive transport soldiers, transport soldiers deceive officials, officials deceive the Son of Heaven—turn by turn deceiving one another—the grain has already become chaff like sand and soil;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover commoners cheat transport soldiers, transport soldiers cheat officials, officials cheat the Son of Heaven—each deceiving the next—until the grain is chaff and sand;

sentences.zh: 兼濕熱蒸變，食不可咽，是又化有用之六，為無用之一矣。

translations.literal: together with damp heat steaming and changing until it cannot be swallowed—thus again turning the useful six into the useless one.
translations.idiomatic: and damp heat spoils it until it cannot be swallowed—turning the six parts the people pay into the one part that is useless.

sentences.zh: 臣以為莫如修屯政，屯政修則地辟而民有樂土，粟積而人有固誌。

translations.literal: Your subject thinks nothing is better than repairing military colony policy; when colony policy is repaired, land is opened and the people have happy soil, grain is stored and people have firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: I believe nothing is better than restoring military colony policy; with colonies restored, land is opened and the people have a secure livelihood, grain is stored and men have firm purpose.

sentences.zh: 昔吳璘守天水，縱橫鑿渠，綿亙不絕，名曰「地網」，敵騎不能逞。

translations.literal: Formerly Wu Lin defended Tianshui, cutting channels crisscross in all directions, continuous without break, called the "earth net"—enemy cavalry could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Lin held Tianshui he cut canals in every direction without cease, calling the network the "earth net," so enemy cavalry could not advance.

sentences.zh: 今仿其制，溝塗之界，各樹土所宜木，小可獲薪果之饒，大可得抗扼之利，敵雖強，何施乎。

translations.literal: Now imitate his system: at the borders of ditches and paths, plant in each place trees suited to the soil—small ones can yield abundance of fuel and fruit, large ones can obtain the advantage of resistance and restraint; though the enemy be strong, what can they do?
translations.idiomatic: Imitate that system today: along ditches and roads plant trees suited to each soil—small ones for fuel and fruit, large ones to block the enemy; however strong the foe, what can he do?

sentences.zh: 帝亟下所司，而議竟中格。

translations.literal: The emperor urgently sent it down to the relevant offices, but the proposal in the end was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor quickly referred it to the relevant offices, but the proposal was ultimately blocked.

sentences.zh: 稍進右給事中。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted right supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to right supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 五年九月，御史智鋌劾學龍及編修侯恪為東林鷹犬，遂削籍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year, investigating censor Zhi Ting impeached Xuelong and compiler Hou Ke as Eastern Forest hawks and hounds, and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifth year Investigating Censor Zhi Ting impeached Xuelong and Compiler Hou Ke as Eastern Forest henchmen, and Xuelong was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年起歷戶科都給事中。

translations.literal: From the first year of Chongzhen he rose through chief supervising secretary of the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: From the first year of Chongzhen he served as chief supervising secretary of the Department of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以民貧盜起，請大清吏治。

translations.literal: Because the people were poor and bandits arose, he asked for a great cleansing of official discipline.
translations.idiomatic: With the people impoverished and bandits rising, he asked for a thorough cleansing of official discipline.

sentences.zh: 尋劾薊撫王應豸克餉激變，又上足餉十六事。

translations.literal: Soon he impeached Jizhou grand coordinator Wang Yingzhi for withholding rations and inciting mutiny, and also submitted sixteen items on sufficient rations.
translations.idiomatic: He soon impeached Jizhou Grand Coordinator Wang Yingzhi for withholding pay and inciting mutiny, and submitted sixteen proposals on adequate rations.

sentences.zh: 帝皆采納。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted them all.

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿、太仆卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 五年改右僉都御史，巡撫江西。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was changed to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「臣所部州縣七十八，而坐逋賦降罰者至九十人。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In the prefectures and counties under my jurisdiction, seventy-eight in number, yet those demoted and punished for sitting on tax arrears reach ninety persons.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "My jurisdiction has seventy-eight prefectures and counties, yet ninety officials have been demoted or punished for tax arrears.

sentences.zh: 由數歲之逋責於一歲，數人之逋責於一人，故終無及額之日也。

translations.literal: Because several years' arrears are charged to one year and several persons' arrears to one person, therefore in the end there is never a day of meeting the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Because several years' arrears are charged to a single year and several men's arrears to a single man, quotas can never be met.

sentences.zh: 請別新舊，酌多寡，立帶征之法。

translations.literal: I ask to distinguish new from old, weigh more and less, and establish a method of collecting arrears in installments.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that old and new arrears be distinguished, amounts weighed, and a method of installment collection established.

sentences.zh: 」可之。

translations.literal: " This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " This was approved.

sentences.zh: 四方盜賊蜂起，江西獨無重兵，學龍以為言，詔增置千人。

translations.literal: Bandits rose everywhere like bees; Jiangxi alone had no heavy troops; Xuelong spoke on this and an edict added one thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits swarmed everywhere, but Jiangxi alone lacked substantial troops; Xuelong raised the matter and an edict added one thousand men.

sentences.zh: 討平都昌、萍鄉諸盜，合閩兵擊破封山妖賊張普薇等，賊遂殄滅。

translations.literal: He suppressed bandits in Duchang, Pingxiang, and elsewhere, joined Fujian troops to defeat the demonic bandits of Fengshan Zhang Puwei and others, and the bandits were then exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified bandits in Duchang, Pingxiang, and elsewhere, joined Fujian troops to defeat the Fengshan rebels led by Zhang Puwei, and the bandits were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 十二年冬，擢南京兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twelfth year he was promoted vice minister of war on the right at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twelfth year he was made vice minister of war on the right at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 明年春，將解任，遵例薦舉屬吏，並及遷謫官黃道周。

translations.literal: The next spring, about to leave office, following precedent he recommended subordinate officials, including also the transferred and banished official Huang Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring, as he was about to leave office, he followed precedent in recommending subordinates, including the banished official Huang Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，征下獄，責其黨庇行私，廷杖八十，削其籍，移入詔獄，竟坐遣戍。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, summoned and put him in prison, blamed him for factional favoritism and private conduct, gave him eighty blows at court, struck his name from the rolls, moved him to the imperial prison, and in the end was sentenced to banishment to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, summoned him to prison, charged factional favoritism, gave him eighty blows at court, struck his name from the rolls, moved him to the imperial prison, and finally banished him to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 十五年秋，道周召還，半道請釋學龍，不聽。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifteenth year Daozhou was recalled; halfway he asked to release Xuelong, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifteenth year Daozhou was recalled; halfway he asked that Xuelong be released, but the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 十七年五月，福王立於南京，召拜兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year the Prince of Fu was established at Nanjing and summoned him as left vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year the Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing and summoned him as left vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 十月擢刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was promoted Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was made Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時方治從賊之獄，仿唐制六等定罪。

translations.literal: At the time they were handling cases of those who followed the bandits, imitating the Tang system's six grades of sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then trying those who had served the rebels, following the Tang system's six grades of punishment.

sentences.zh: 學龍議定，以十二月上之：

translations.literal: Xuelong settled the deliberations and in the twelfth month submitted them:
translations.idiomatic: Xuelong finalized the sentences and submitted them in the twelfth month:

sentences.zh: 其一等應磔者：吏部員外郎宋企郊，舉人牛金星，平陽知府張嶙然，太仆少卿曹欽程，御史李振聲、喻上猷，山西提學參議黎誌升，陜西左布政使陸之祺，兵科給事中高翔漢，潼關道僉事楊王休，翰林院檢討劉世芳十一人也。

translations.literal: First grade, to be dismembered: Department of Personnel vice director Song Qijiao, provincial graduate Niu Jinxing, Pingyang prefect Zhang Linran, Court of the Imperial Stud vice minister Cao Qincheng, investigating censors Li Zhensheng and Yu Shangyou, Shanxi education intendant Li Zhisheng, Shaanxi left administration commissioner Lu Zhiqi, Department of War supervising secretary Gao Xianghan, Tongguan circuit vice commissioner Yang Wangxiu, and Hanlin Academy reviser Liu Shifang—eleven persons.
translations.idiomatic: First grade, death by dismemberment: Vice Director Song Qijiao of the Ministry of Personnel, provincial graduate Niu Jinxing, Prefect Zhang Linran of Pingyang, Vice Minister Cao Qincheng of the Court of the Imperial Stud, investigating censors Li Zhensheng and Yu Shangyou, Shanxi Education Intendant Li Zhisheng, Shaanxi Administration Commissioner Lu Zhiqi, Supervising Secretary Gao Xianghan of the Department of War, Tongguan Vice Commissioner Yang Wangxiu, and Hanlin Reviser Liu Shifang—eleven men in all.

sentences.zh: 二等應斬秋決者：刑科給事中光時亨，河南提學僉事鞏焴，庶吉士周鍾，兵部主事方允昌四人也。

translations.literal: Second grade, to be beheaded at autumn execution: Department of Justice supervising secretary Guang Shiheng, Henan education vice commissioner Gong Huang, Hanlin bachelor Zhou Zhong, and Ministry of War principal clerk Fang Yunchang—four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Second grade, beheading at the autumn assizes: Supervising Secretary Guang Shiheng of the Department of Justice, Henan Education Vice Commissioner Gong Huang, Hanlin bachelor Zhou Zhong, and Principal Clerk Fang Yunchang of the Ministry of War—four men.

sentences.zh: 三等應絞擬贖者：翰林修撰兼戶、兵二科都給事中陳名復，戶科給事中楊枝起、廖國遴，襄陽知府王承曾，天津兵備副使原毓宗，庶吉士何胤光，少詹事項煜七人也。

translations.literal: Third grade, strangulation with commutation to ransom: Hanlin compiler concurrently chief supervising secretary of the Departments of Revenue and War Chen Mingfu, Department of Revenue supervising secretaries Yang Zhiqi and Liao Guolin, Xiangyang prefect Wang Chengzeng, Tianjin military defense vice commissioner Yuan Yuzong, Hanlin bachelor He Yinguang, and junior mentor Xiang Yu—seven persons.
translations.idiomatic: Third grade, strangulation commutable to ransom: Hanlin Compiler Chen Mingfu, concurrently chief supervising secretary of the Departments of Revenue and War; Supervising Secretaries Yang Zhiqi and Liao Guolin of the Department of Revenue; Prefect Wang Chengzeng of Xiangyang; Tianjin Military Defense Vice Commissioner Yuan Yuzong; Hanlin bachelor He Yinguang; and Junior Mentor Xiang Yu—seven men.

sentences.zh: 四等應戍擬贖者：禮部主事王孫蕙，翰林院檢討梁兆陽，大理寺正錢位坤，總督侍郎侯恂，山西副使王秉鑒，御史陳羽白、裴希度、張懋爵，禮部郎中劉大鞏，吏部員外郎郭萬象，給事中申芝芳、金汝礪，舉人吳達，修撰揚廷鑒及黃繼祖十五人也。

translations.literal: Fourth grade, banishment with commutation to ransom: Ministry of Rites principal clerk Wang Sunhui, Hanlin reviser Liang Zhaoyang, Court of Judicial Review director Qian Weikun, grand coordinator vice minister Hou Xun, Shanxi vice commissioner Wang Bingjian, investigating censors Chen Yubai, Pei Xidu, and Zhang Maojue, Ministry of Rites director Liu Dagong, Department of Personnel vice director Guo Wanxiang, supervising secretaries Shen Zhifang and Jin Ruli, provincial graduate Wu Da, compiler Yang Tingjian, and Huang Jizu—fifteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth grade, banishment commutable to ransom: Principal Clerk Wang Sunhui of the Ministry of Rites; Hanlin Reviser Liang Zhaoyang; Director Qian Weikun of the Court of Judicial Review; Grand Coordinator Vice Minister Hou Xun; Shanxi Vice Commissioner Wang Bingjian; investigating censors Chen Yubai, Pei Xidu, and Zhang Maojue; Director Liu Dagong of the Ministry of Rites; Vice Director Guo Wanxiang of the Ministry of Personnel; supervising secretaries Shen Zhifang and Jin Ruli; provincial graduate Wu Da; Compiler Yang Tingjian; and Huang Jizu—fifteen men.

sentences.zh: 五等應徒擬贖者：通政司參議宋學顯，諭德方拱乾，工部主事繆沅，給事中呂兆龍、傅振鐸，進士吳剛思，檢討方以智、傅鼎銓，庶吉士張家玉及沈元龍十人也。

translations.literal: Fifth grade, penal servitude with commutation to ransom: Office of Transmission vice commissioner Song Xuexian, tutor Fang Gongqian, Ministry of Works principal clerk Miao Yuan, supervising secretaries Lü Zhaolong and Fu Zhenduo, jinshi Wu Gangsi, revisers Fang Yizhi and Fu Dingquan, Hanlin bachelors Zhang Jiayu and Shen Yuanlong—ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth grade, penal servitude commutable to ransom: Vice Commissioner Song Xuexian of the Office of Transmission; Tutor Fang Gongqian; Principal Clerk Miao Yuan of the Ministry of Works; supervising secretaries Lü Zhaolong and Fu Zhenduo; jinshi Wu Gangsi; revisers Fang Yizhi and Fu Dingquan; Hanlin bachelors Zhang Jiayu and Shen Yuanlong—ten men.

sentences.zh: 六等應杖擬贖者：工部員外郎潘同春，禮部員外郎吳泰來，主事張琦，行人王於曜，行取知縣周壽明，進士徐家麒及向列星、李八人也。

translations.literal: Sixth grade, beating with commutation to ransom: Ministry of Works vice director Pan Tongchun, Ministry of Rites vice director Wu Tailai, principal clerk Zhang Qi, courier Wang Yuyao, selected magistrate Zhou Shouming, jinshi Xu Jiaqi, and Xiang Liexing and Li Huang—eight persons.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth grade, beating commutable to ransom: Vice Director Pan Tongchun of the Ministry of Works; Vice Director Wu Tailai of the Ministry of Rites; Principal Clerk Zhang Qi; Courier Wang Yuyao; selected magistrate Zhou Shouming; jinshi Xu Jiaqi; and Xiang Liexing and Li Huang—eight men.

sentences.zh: 其留北俟後定奪者：少詹事何瑞征、楊觀光，太仆少卿張若麒，副使方大猷，戶部侍郎黨崇雅，吏部侍郎熊文舉，太仆卿葉初春，給事中龔鼎孳、戴明說、孫承澤、劉昌，御史塗必泓、張鳴駿，司業薛所蘊，通政參議趙京仕，編修高爾儼，戶部郎中衛周祚及黃紀、孫襄十九人也。

translations.literal: Those remaining in the north awaiting later final decision: junior mentors He Ruizheng and Yang Guanguang, Court of the Imperial Stud vice minister Zhang Ruoqi, vice commissioner Fang Dayou, Ministry of Revenue vice minister Dang Chongya, Department of Personnel vice minister Xiong Wenju, Court of the Imperial Stud minister Ye Chuchun, supervising secretaries Gong Dingzi, Dai Mingshuo, Sun Chengze, and Liu Chang, investigating censors Tu Bihong and Zhang Mingjun, director of studies Xue Suoyun, Office of Transmission vice commissioner Zhao Jingshi, compiler Gao Eryan, Ministry of Revenue director Wei Zhouzuo, and Huang Ji and Sun Xiang—nineteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: Those who remained in the north pending later decision: Junior Mentors He Ruizheng and Yang Guanguang; Vice Minister Zhang Ruoqi of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Vice Commissioner Fang Dayou; Vice Minister Dang Chongya of the Ministry of Revenue; Vice Minister Xiong Wenju of the Ministry of Personnel; Minister Ye Chuchun of the Court of the Imperial Stud; supervising secretaries Gong Dingzi, Dai Mingshuo, Sun Chengze, and Liu Chang; investigating censors Tu Bihong and Zhang Mingjun; Director of Studies Xue Suoyun; Vice Commissioner Zhao Jingshi of the Office of Transmission; Compiler Gao Eryan; Director Wei Zhouzuo of the Ministry of Revenue; and Huang Ji and Sun Xiang—nineteen men.

sentences.zh: 其另存再議者：給事中翁元益、郭充、庶吉士魯、吳爾壎、史可程、王自超、白胤謙、梁清標、楊棲鶚、張元琳、呂崇烈、李化麟、朱積、趙颎、劉廷琮，吏部郎中侯佐，員外郎左懋泰，禮部郎中吳之琦，兵部員外郎鄒明魁，行人許作梅，進士胡顯，太常博士龔懋熙及王之牧、王臯、梅鶚、姬琨、朱國壽、吳嵩胤二十八人也。

translations.literal: Those separately kept for further deliberation: supervising secretaries Weng Yuanyi and Guo Chong, Hanlin bachelors Lu [character unclear], Wu Erxun, Shi Kecheng, Wang Zichao, Bai Yinqian, Liang Qingbiao, Yang Qie, Zhang Yuanlin, Lü Chonglie, Li Hualin, Zhu Ji, Zhao Jiong, and Liu Tingcong, Department of Personnel director Hou Zuo, vice director Zuo Maotai, Ministry of Rites director Wu Zhiqi, Ministry of War vice director Zou Mingkui, courier Xu Zuomei, jinshi Hu Xian, Court of Imperial Sacrifices erudite Gong Maoxi, and Wang Zhimu, Wang Gao, Mei E, Ji Kun, Zhu Guoshou, and Wu Songyin—twenty-eight persons.
translations.idiomatic: Those set aside for further deliberation: Supervising Secretaries Weng Yuanyi and Guo Chong; Hanlin bachelors Lu [character unclear], Wu Erxun, Shi Kecheng, Wang Zichao, Bai Yinqian, Liang Qingbiao, Yang Qie, Zhang Yuanlin, Lü Chonglie, Li Hualin, Zhu Ji, Zhao Jiong, and Liu Tingcong; Director Hou Zuo of the Ministry of Personnel; Vice Director Zuo Maotai; Director Wu Zhiqi of the Ministry of Rites; Vice Director Zou Mingkui of the Ministry of War; Courier Xu Zuomei; jinshi Hu Xian; Erudite Gong Maoxi of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; and Wang Zhimu, Wang Gao, Mei E, Ji Kun, Zhu Guoshou, and Wu Songyin—twenty-eight men.

sentences.zh: 其已奉旨錄用者：兵部尚書張縉彥，給事中時敏，諭德衛胤文、韓四維，御史蘇京，行取知縣黃國琦、施鳳儀，兵部郎中張正聲，內閣中書舍人顧大成及姜荃林等十人也。

translations.literal: Those already by imperial decree recorded for employment: Minister of War Zhang Jinyan, supervising secretary Shi Min, tutors Wei Yinwen and Han Siwei, investigating censor Su Jing, selected magistrates Huang Guoqi and Shi Fengyi, Ministry of War director Zhang Zhengsheng, Grand Secretariat secretarial clerk Gu Dacheng, and Jiang Quanlin and others—ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: Those already appointed by imperial decree: Minister of War Zhang Jinyan; Supervising Secretary Shi Min; Tutors Wei Yinwen and Han Siwei; Investigating Censor Su Jing; selected magistrates Huang Guoqi and Shi Fengyi; Director Zhang Zhengsheng of the Ministry of War; Grand Secretariat Clerk Gu Dacheng; and Jiang Quanlin and others—ten men.

sentences.zh: 得旨：「周鍾等不當緩決，陳名夏等未蔽厥辜，侯恂、宋學顯、吳剛思、方以智、潘同春等擬罪未合。

translations.literal: Receiving the rescript: "Zhou Zhong and others should not be given delayed execution; Chen Mingxia and others have not covered their guilt; Hou Xun, Song Xuexian, Wu Gangsi, Fang Yizhi, Pan Tongchun, and others—the proposed crimes do not fit.
translations.idiomatic: The rescript read: "Zhou Zhong and others should not receive delayed execution; Chen Mingxia and others have not yet paid for their crimes; the sentences proposed for Hou Xun, Song Xuexian, Wu Gangsi, Fang Yizhi, Pan Tongchun, and others do not fit the offenses.

sentences.zh: 新榜進士盡汙偽命，不當復玷班聯。

translations.literal: New-list jinshi are all stained by false commands and should not again defile the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Newly listed jinshi are all tainted by the rebel regime and must not again hold court rank.

sentences.zh: 」令再議。

translations.literal: " Order further deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " Order further deliberation.

sentences.zh: 惟方拱乾結納馬、阮，特旨免其罪。

translations.literal: Only Fang Gongqian, having connected with Ma and Ruan, received a special edict exempting him from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Only Fang Gongqian, who had cultivated Ma and Ruan, received a special edict exempting him from punishment.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，學龍奉詔擬周鍾、光時亨等各加一等，潘同春諸臣皆侯補小臣，受偽無據，仍執前律。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year, Xuelong by imperial decree proposed Zhou Zhong, Guang Shiheng, and others each increased one grade; Pan Tongchun and the various officials were all minor officials awaiting appointment, with no evidence of accepting the false regime, and still held to the previous statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the next year Xuelong, by imperial order, proposed raising Zhou Zhong, Guang Shiheng, and others one grade each; Pan Tongchun and the rest were minor officials awaiting appointment, with no evidence they had served the rebels, and he still applied the earlier statutes.

sentences.zh: 當是時，馬、阮必欲殺周鍾。

translations.literal: At this time Ma and Ruan were determined to kill Zhou Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ma and Ruan were determined to kill Zhou Zhong.

sentences.zh: 學龍欲緩其死，謀之次輔王鐸，乘士英註籍上之，且請停刑。

translations.literal: Xuelong wished to delay his death, consulted second Grand Secretary Wang Duo, and while Shiying was registering his credentials submitted it, also asking to suspend execution.
translations.idiomatic: Xuelong wished to spare him, consulted Second Grand Secretary Wang Duo, and submitted the memorial while Shiying was registering his credentials, also asking that execution be suspended.

sentences.zh: 鐸即擬俞旨，褒以詳慎平允。

translations.literal: Duo at once drafted an approving rescript, praising it as detailed, cautious, and even-handed.
translations.idiomatic: Duo at once drafted an approving rescript, praising the proposal as thorough, cautious, and fair.

sentences.zh: 士英聞之大怒，然事已無及。

translations.literal: Shiying on hearing was greatly angry, but the matter was already beyond remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying was furious when he heard, but it was already too late.

sentences.zh: 大鋮暨其黨張捷、楊維垣聲言欲劾學龍，學龍引疾。

translations.literal: Ruan Dacheng and his faction Zhang Jie and Yang Weiyuan openly declared they would impeach Xuelong; Xuelong cited illness.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Dacheng and his allies Zhang Jie and Yang Weiyuan openly threatened to impeach Xuelong; Xuelong pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 命未下，保國公朱國弼、御史張孫振等詆其曲庇行私，遂削籍。

translations.literal: Before the order came down, Defender of the State Zhu Guobi, investigating censor Zhang Sunzhen, and others reviled him for warped favoritism and private conduct, and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Before the order came down, Defender of the State Zhu Guobi, Investigating Censor Zhang Sunzhen, and others accused him of favoritism and private dealing, and he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 大鋮既殺鍾、時亨，即傳旨二等罪斬者謫允充南金齒軍，三等罪絞者充廣西邊衛軍，四等以下俱為民，永不敘用。

translations.literal: Dacheng having killed Zhong and Shiheng, at once transmitted an edict: those of second-grade beheading were banished to serve as soldiers in southern Jinchijun, those of third-grade strangulation to serve as soldiers in Guangxi frontier guards, fourth grade and below all made commoners, never again employed.
translations.idiomatic: After Dacheng had killed Zhong and Shiheng, he issued an edict: those sentenced to second-grade beheading were banished to serve in southern Jinchijun; those sentenced to third-grade strangulation to serve in Guangxi frontier guards; fourth grade and below were made commoners and never again employed.

sentences.zh: 然學龍所定案亦多漏網，而所擬一等諸犯，皆隨賊西行，實未嘗正刑辟也。

translations.literal: Yet in the cases Xuelong settled many also escaped the net, and those he proposed for first grade all followed the bandits westward—in fact they never underwent proper capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet many in Xuelong's list also escaped justice, and those he had sentenced to the first grade all followed the rebels west—in fact none ever underwent formal execution.

sentences.zh: 黃繼祖、沈元龍、向列星、李、黃紀、孫襄、王之牧、王臯、梅鶚、姬琨、朱國壽、吳嵩胤、姜荃林，皆未詳其官。

translations.literal: Huang Jizu, Shen Yuanlong, Xiang Liexing, Li Huang, Huang Ji, Sun Xiang, Wang Zhimu, Wang Gao, Mei E, Ji Kun, Zhu Guoshou, Wu Songyin, and Jiang Quanlin—their offices are all not detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jizu, Shen Yuanlong, Xiang Liexing, Li Huang, Huang Ji, Sun Xiang, Wang Zhimu, Wang Gao, Mei E, Ji Kun, Zhu Guoshou, Wu Songyin, and Jiang Quanlin—their offices are not recorded in detail.

sentences.zh: 學龍歸，南都旋失。

translations.literal: Xuelong returned home; the Southern Capital soon perished.
translations.idiomatic: Xuelong went home; the Southern Capital soon fell.

sentences.zh: 久之卒於家。

translations.literal: After a long time he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home some years later.

sentences.zh: 高倬，字枝樓，忠州人。

translations.literal: Gao Zhuo, styled Zhilou, was a native of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhuo, courtesy name Zhilou, was from Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the fifth year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifth year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 除德清知縣，調金華。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Deqing and transferred to Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Deqing and later transferred to Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，征授御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was summoned and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was summoned and made investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 薊遼總督曹文衡與總監鄧希詔相訐奏。

translations.literal: Jiliao grand coordinator Cao Wenheng and grand supervisor Deng Xizhao mutually impeached each other in memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Jiliao Grand Coordinator Cao Wenheng and Grand Supervisor Deng Xizhao impeached each other in competing memorials.

sentences.zh: 詔殫力幹濟，以副委任。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them to exert their utmost in practical achievement to fulfill the commission.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered them to exert themselves fully to fulfill their commissions.

sentences.zh: 倬乃上疏言：「文衡骯臟成性，必不能仰鼻息於中官；

translations.literal: Zhuo then memorialized: "Wenheng is by nature proud and defiled and surely cannot breathe at the mercy of eunuchs;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo then wrote: "Wenheng is proud and corrupt by nature and cannot submit to breathing at eunuchs' pleasure;

sentences.zh: 希詔睚眥未忘，何能化戈矛為同氣。

translations.literal: Xizhao has not forgotten a grudge the size of a eyelash—how can he turn spears and shields into shared breath?
translations.idiomatic: Xizhao has not forgotten the slightest grudge—how can they turn enemies into allies?

sentences.zh: 封疆事重，宜撤希詔安文衡心。

translations.literal: Frontier affairs are weighty; Xizhao should be removed to settle Wenheng's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier affairs are grave; Xizhao should be removed to reassure Wenheng.

sentences.zh: 若文衡不足用，宜更置，勿使中官參之。

translations.literal: If Wenheng is not fit for use, another should be appointed; do not let eunuchs participate.
translations.idiomatic: If Wenheng is unfit for the post, replace him—but do not let eunuchs interfere.

sentences.zh: 諸邊鎮臣如希詔不少，使人效希詔，督撫之展布益難。

translations.literal: Frontier garrison officials like Xizhao are not few; if people imitate Xizhao, grand coordinators' deployment becomes all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: There are many frontier garrison officials like Xizhao; if others imitate him, grand coordinators will find it still harder to command.

sentences.zh: 即諸邊督撫如文衡亦不少，使人效文衡，將邊事之廢壞愈甚。

translations.literal: Likewise frontier grand coordinators like Wenheng are not few; if people imitate Wenheng, frontier affairs will be ruined all the more.
translations.idiomatic: There are also many frontier grand coordinators like Wenheng; if others imitate him, frontier affairs will collapse all the faster.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，貶一秩視事。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, he was demoted one rank and continued in office.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived he was demoted one rank but kept his post.

sentences.zh: 巡視草場，坐失火下吏。

translations.literal: Inspecting pasture lands, he was sent down to officials for a fire.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting pasture lands he was prosecuted for a fire.

sentences.zh: 廷臣申救，不納。

translations.literal: Court officials pleaded for him; this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials pleaded for him; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 逾年熱審，給事中吳甘來以為言，始釋歸。

translations.literal: After a year at the summer review, supervising secretary Wu Ganlai spoke on his behalf, and he was at last released to return.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, at the summer review, Supervising Secretary Wu Ganlai spoke for him and he was at last released.

sentences.zh: 起上林署丞，稍遷大理右寺副。

translations.literal: He was recalled as assistant director of the Imperial Park Office and soon promoted deputy director of the right division of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as assistant director of the Imperial Park Office and soon promoted deputy director of the right division of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 十一年五月，火星逆行，詔修省。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year Mars moved retrograde and an edict ordered self-examination and reform.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eleventh year Mars moved retrograde and the court ordered self-examination and reform.

sentences.zh: 倬以近者刑獄滋繁，法官務停閣，請敕諸司克期奏報，大者旬，小者五日。

translations.literal: Zhuo, because recently criminal cases had grown numerous and judges strove to delay, asked that all offices be ordered to report by set deadlines—ten days for major cases, five for minor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo noted that criminal cases had multiplied and judges were stalling; he asked that all offices be ordered to report by deadline—ten days for major cases, five for minor.

sentences.zh: 其奉旨覆讞者，或五日三日，務俾積案盡疏，囹圄衰減。

translations.literal: Those who received imperial command to review sentences should do so in five or three days, striving to clear all accumulated cases and reduce the prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Cases sent back for review should be decided in five or three days, so that backlog is cleared and the prisons emptied.

sentences.zh: 帝為采納。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 屢遷南京太仆卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 太仆故駐滁州，滁為南都西北門戶。

translations.literal: The Imperial Stud was formerly stationed at Chuzhou; Chuzhou was the northwestern gateway of the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Stud was stationed at Chuzhou, the northwestern gateway to the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 請募州人為兵，保障鄉土，從之。

translations.literal: He asked to recruit men of the prefecture as soldiers to protect the native soil; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to recruit local men as soldiers to defend the region; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 十六年二月擢右僉都御史，提督操江。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixteenth year he was promoted right vice censor-in-chief and put in charge of training the Yangzi forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixteenth year he was made right vice censor-in-chief and put in charge of training the Yangzi forces.

sentences.zh: 其秋，操江改任武臣劉孔昭，召倬別用，未赴而京師陷。

translations.literal: That autumn training the Yangzi was changed to the military officer Liu Kongzhao; Zhuo was summoned for other employment but had not gone when the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Yangzi command was given to the military officer Liu Kongzhao; Zhuo was summoned elsewhere but had not taken up the post when the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 福王立南京，拜倬工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu was established at Nanjing and appointed Zhuo vice minister of works on the right.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing, Zhuo was made vice minister of works on the right.

sentences.zh: 禦用監內官請給工料銀，置龍鳳幾榻諸器物及宮殿陳設金玉諸寶，計貲數十萬，倬請裁省。

translations.literal: Eunuchs of the Imperial Supplies Office asked for silver for materials to make dragon-and-phoenix tables, couches, and other objects and palace furnishings of gold, jade, and treasures, costing several hundred thousand; Zhuo asked to cut and reduce.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs of the Imperial Supplies Office asked for silver to make dragon-and-phoenix furnishings and palace ornaments in gold and jade, costing several hundred thousand taels; Zhuo asked that the expense be cut.

sentences.zh: 光祿寺辦禦用器至萬五千七百有奇，倬又以為言。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrificial Wine prepared imperial utensils reaching more than fifteen thousand seven hundred odd; Zhuo again spoke on this.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrificial Wine was preparing more than fifteen thousand seven hundred imperial utensils; Zhuo protested again.

sentences.zh: 皆不納。

translations.literal: None was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: None of his protests was heeded.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，由左侍郎拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year, from left vice minister he was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the next year he was promoted from left vice minister to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 國破，倬投繯死。

translations.literal: When the state perished, Zhuo hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty fell, Zhuo hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 是時，大臣殉難者：倬與張捷、楊維垣、庶僚則有黃端伯、劉成治、吳嘉胤、龔廷祥。

translations.literal: At this time great ministers who died for the calamity: Zhuo with Zhang Jie and Yang Weiyuan; among lower officials Huang Duanbo, Liu Chengzhi, Wu Jiayin, and Gong Tingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Among the chief ministers who died for the cause were Zhuo, Zhang Jie, and Yang Weiyuan; among lower officials Huang Duanbo, Liu Chengzhi, Wu Jiayin, and Gong Tingxiang.

sentences.zh: 成治，字廣如，漢陽人。

translations.literal: Chengzhi, styled Guangru, was a native of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chengzhi, courtesy name Guangru, was from Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the seventh year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the seventh year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 福王時，歷官戶部郎中。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu he rose to director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he served as director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 國破，忻城伯趙之龍將出降，入戶部封府庫。

translations.literal: When the state perished, Baron of Xincheng Zhao Zhilong was about to surrender and entered the Ministry of Revenue to seal the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty fell, Baron of Xincheng Zhao Zhilong was about to surrender and went to the Ministry of Revenue to seal the treasury.

sentences.zh: 成治憤，手搏之，之龍跳而免。

translations.literal: Chengzhi in rage grappled with him hand to hand; Zhilong leaped away and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi in fury seized him; Zhilong broke free and fled.

sentences.zh: 成治自經。

translations.literal: Chengzhi hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 嘉胤，字繩如，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Jiayin, styled Shengru, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jiayin, courtesy name Shengru, was from Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 由鄉舉歷官戶部主事。

translations.literal: Through provincial recommendation he rose to principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Through the provincial examination he rose to principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 奉使出都，聞變，還謁方孝孺祠，投繯死。

translations.literal: On mission he left the capital; hearing of the calamity he returned, visited the shrine of Fang Xiaoru, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: On official business he had left the capital; hearing of the fall he returned, visited the shrine of Fang Xiaoru, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 廷祥，字伯興，無錫人。

translations.literal: Tingxiang, styled Boxing, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Tingxiang, courtesy name Boxing, was from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 馬世奇門人也。

translations.literal: He was a disciple of Ma Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: He was a disciple of Ma Shiqi.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 為中書舍人。

translations.literal: He served as secretarial clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a secretarial clerk of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 城破，衣冠步至武定橋投水死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, in cap and gown he walked to Wuding Bridge and threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he walked in cap and gown to Wuding Bridge and drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 時又有欽天監博士陳於階、國子生吳可箕、武舉黃金璽、布衣陳士達，並死焉。

translations.literal: At the time there were also Imperial Observatory erudite Chen Yujie, National University student Wu Keji, military examination graduate Huang Jinxi, and commoner Chen Shida—all died likewise.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Imperial Observatory Erudite Chen Yujie, National University student Wu Keji, military examination graduate Huang Jinxi, and commoner Chen Shida also died.

sentences.zh: 左懋第，字蘿石，萊陽人。

translations.literal: Zuo Maodi, styled Luoshi, was a native of Laiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Maodi, courtesy name Luoshi, was from Laiyang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the fourth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fourth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 授韓城知縣，有異政。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Hancheng and had outstanding administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Hancheng and governed with distinction.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪，三年不入內寢，事母盡孝。

translations.literal: He suffered his father's death, for three years did not enter the inner chamber, and served his mother with full filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he observed mourning for three years without entering the inner chamber and served his mother with full devotion.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢戶科給事中。
