translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted supervising secretary in the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made supervising secretary in the Department of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 疏陳四弊，謂民困、兵弱、臣工委頓、國計虛耗也。

translations.literal: He memorialized setting forth four abuses: the people's distress, military weakness, exhaustion of officials, and empty drain of state finances.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on four abuses: popular distress, military weakness, official exhaustion, and empty drain on state finances.

sentences.zh: 又陳貴粟之策，令天下贖罪者盡輸粟，鹽筴復開中之舊，令輸粟邊塞充軍食。

translations.literal: He also set forth a policy of valuing grain, ordering all who ransomed crimes nationwide to pay grain, restoring the old kaizhong system for the salt monopoly, and ordering grain paid to frontier garrisons for military food.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed valuing grain: all who paid fines should pay in grain; the salt monopoly should restore the old kaizhong system, with grain delivered to frontier garrisons for military rations.

sentences.zh: 彗星見，詔停刑，懋第請馬上速傳。

translations.literal: A comet appeared and an edict halted executions; Maodi asked that it be swiftly transmitted by relay.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared the court halted executions; Maodi asked that the edict be relayed at once.

sentences.zh: 又請嚴禁將士剽掠，有司朘削。

translations.literal: He also asked strictly to forbid soldiers and officers from plundering and officials from squeezing.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that plunder by troops and squeezing by officials be strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 請散米錢，振輦下饑民，收養嬰孩。

translations.literal: He asked to distribute grain and money, relieve hungry people around the capital, and take in infants.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that grain and money be distributed to relieve famine around the capital and that infants be taken in.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，剿餉罷征，亦請馬上速行，恐遠方吏不知，先已征，民不沾實惠。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year suppression rations were halted; he also asked swift execution by relay, fearing distant officials would not know and collect first, so the people would not receive the real benefit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the next year suppression levies were halted; he again asked immediate relay, fearing distant officials would collect before hearing the order and the people would receive no real relief.

sentences.zh: 帝並采納。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted them all.

sentences.zh: 三月，大風霾。

translations.literal: In the third month, great wind and haze.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month came great winds and haze.

sentences.zh: 帝布袍齋居，禱之不止。

translations.literal: The emperor wore plain cloth and dwelt in fasting quarters, praying without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore plain cloth and fasted, praying without cease.

sentences.zh: 懋第言：「去秋星變，朝停刑而夕即滅。

translations.literal: Maodi said: "Last autumn when the stars changed, executions were halted in the morning and by evening they had vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Maodi said: "Last autumn when the stars changed, the court halted executions in the morning and by evening the omen had vanished.

sentences.zh: 今者不然，豈陛下有其文未修其實乎？

translations.literal: Now it is not so—has Your Majesty the form but not repaired the substance?
translations.idiomatic: Now it is not so—has Your Majesty kept the form but not the substance?

sentences.zh: 臣敢以實進。

translations.literal: Your subject dares advance with substance.
translations.idiomatic: I dare speak to the substance.

sentences.zh: 練餉之加，原非得已。

translations.literal: The addition of training rations originally could not be helped.
translations.idiomatic: The training levy was originally unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 乃明旨減兵以省餉，天下共知之，而餉猶未省，何也？

translations.literal: Yet a clear edict reduced troops to save rations—the whole realm knows this—yet rations are still not saved; why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet a clear edict ordered troop reductions to save pay—the whole realm knows it—yet pay is still not reduced; why?

sentences.zh: 請自今因兵征餉，預使天下知應加之數，官吏無所逞其奸，以信陛下之明詔。

translations.literal: I ask that from now on when rations are levied because of troops, the realm be told beforehand the amount to be added, so officials have nowhere to practice deceit and Your Majesty's bright edict may be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that henceforth when levies follow troop deployments, the amount be announced in advance so officials cannot cheat and Your Majesty's edict may be trusted.

sentences.zh: 而刑獄則以睿慮之疑信，定諸囚之死生，諸疑於心與疑信半者，悉從輕典。

translations.literal: As for criminal cases, let sagely deliberation's doubt and certainty decide prisoners' life and death; all doubtful in mind or half doubtful and half certain—altogether follow lenient statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In criminal cases let Your Majesty's judgment of doubt and certainty decide life and death; all cases doubtful in your mind, or half doubtful, should follow lenient statutes.

sentences.zh: 豈停刑可止彗，解網不可以返風乎？

translations.literal: Can halting executions stop comets, yet loosening the net not turn back the wind?
translations.idiomatic: If halting executions can stop comets, cannot loosening the net turn back the wind?

sentences.zh: 且陛下屢沛大恩，四方死者猶枕藉，盜賊未見衰止，何也？

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty has repeatedly poured forth great grace, yet the dead in the four quarters still lie piled, and bandits are not seen to weaken and stop—why?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Your Majesty has repeatedly shown great mercy, yet the dead still lie piled across the realm and bandits show no sign of abating—why?

sentences.zh: 由蠲停者止一二。

translations.literal: Because those remitted and halted are only one or two.
translations.idiomatic: Because only one or two levies have truly been remitted.

sentences.zh: 存留之賦，有司迫考成，催征未敢緩，是以莫救於兇荒。

translations.literal: Retained levies—officials pressed by performance review dare not slow collection—therefore nothing saves from fierce famine.
translations.idiomatic: Retained taxes—officials pressed by performance reviews dare not slow collection—so famine cannot be relieved.

sentences.zh: 請於極荒州縣，下詔速停，有司息訟，專以救荒為務。

translations.literal: I ask that in the most famine-stricken prefectures and counties an edict swiftly halt collection, officials cease litigation, and take relief of famine as their sole task.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that in the worst-stricken prefectures and counties an edict halt collection at once, that officials cease litigation, and make famine relief their sole task.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「然。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "So.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "It shall be so.

sentences.zh: 」於是上災七十五州縣新、舊、練三餉並停。

translations.literal: " Thereupon in upper-famine seventy-five prefectures and counties the new, old, and training three rations were all halted.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon in seventy-five prefectures and counties under upper-famine classification, the new, old, and training levies were all halted.

sentences.zh: 中災六十八州縣止征練餉，下災二十八州縣秋成督征。

translations.literal: In middle-famine sixty-eight prefectures and counties only training rations were collected; in lower-famine twenty-eight prefectures and counties collection was supervised after the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: In sixty-eight middle-famine prefectures and counties only the training levy was collected; in twenty-eight lower-famine prefectures and counties collection was deferred until after the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 十四年督催漕運，道中馳疏言：「臣自靜海抵臨清，見人民饑死者三，疫死者三，為盜者四。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he supervised and urged grain transport; on the road he sent a swift memorial: "Your subject from Jinghai to Linqing saw people: three parts starved to death, three parts died of plague, four parts became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he supervised grain transport and sent a swift memorial from the road: "From Jinghai to Linqing I saw the people: three parts starved, three died of plague, four turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 米石銀二十四兩，人死取以食，惟聖明垂念。

translations.literal: Rice was twenty-four taels of silver per shi; the dead were taken for food—I beg the sage brightness to take thought.
translations.idiomatic: Rice cost twenty-four taels per shi; the dead were taken for food—I beg Your Majesty to take thought.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「臣自魚臺至南陽，流寇殺戮，村市為墟。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Your subject from Yutai to Nanyang—roving bandits slaughtered, villages and markets became ruins.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote: "From Yutai to Nanyang roaming bandits slaughtered until villages and markets were ruins.

sentences.zh: 其他饑疫死者，屍積水涯，河為不流，振捄安可不速。

translations.literal: Besides these, the starved and plague-dead—corpses piled at the water's edge, rivers ceased to flow—how can relief not be swift?
translations.idiomatic: Besides these, famine and plague left corpses piled along the waterways until rivers ceased to flow—relief cannot wait.

sentences.zh: 」已又陳安民息盜之策，請核荒田，察逋戶，予以有生之樂，鼓其耕種之心。

translations.literal: " He then also set forth policies to settle the people and quell bandits, asking to verify wasteland, inspect absconded households, give them the joy of living, and rouse their hearts to plow and plant.
translations.idiomatic: " He then proposed policies to pacify the people and quell bandits: verify wasteland, find absconded households, restore their livelihood, and rouse them to farm.

sentences.zh: 又言：「臣有事河干一載，每進父老問疾苦，皆言練餉之害。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your subject has had business along the river for a year; whenever I met elders and asked their hardships, all spoke of the harm of training rations.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "I have worked along the river for a year; whenever I asked elders of their hardships, all spoke of the harm of the training levy.

sentences.zh: 三年來，農怨於野，商嘆於途。

translations.literal: For three years farmers have grieved in the fields and merchants sighed on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: For three years farmers have grieved in the fields and merchants sighed on the roads.

sentences.zh: 如此重派，所練何兵？

translations.literal: With such heavy levies, what troops are being trained?
translations.idiomatic: With such heavy levies, what troops are being trained?

sentences.zh: 兵在何所？

translations.literal: Where are the troops?
translations.idiomatic: Where are they?

sentences.zh: 剿賊禦邊，效安在？

translations.literal: In suppressing bandits and guarding the frontier, where is the effect?
translations.idiomatic: What success in suppressing bandits or guarding the frontier?

sentences.zh: 奈何使眾心瓦解，一至此極乎！

translations.literal: How can popular hearts be dissolved to such an extreme!
translations.idiomatic: How can popular morale be shattered to such a degree!

sentences.zh: 」又言：「臣去冬抵宿遷，見督漕臣史可法，言山東米石二十兩，而河南乃至百五十兩，漕儲多逋。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Your subject last winter reached Suqian and met grain transport supervisor Shi Kefa, who said Shandong rice was twenty taels per shi while Henan reached one hundred fifty, and transport stores were much in arrears.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote: "Last winter I reached Suqian and met grain transport supervisor Shi Kefa, who said Shandong rice was twenty taels per shi while Henan reached one hundred fifty, and transport stores were deeply in arrears.

sentences.zh: 朝議不收折色，需本色。

translations.literal: Court discussion would not accept commuted payment but required grain in kind.
translations.idiomatic: The court would not accept commuted payment but required grain in kind.

sentences.zh: 今淮、鳳間麥大熟，如收兩地折色，易麥轉輸，豈不大利。

translations.literal: Now between Huai and Feng wheat has ripened greatly; if commuted payment were collected in both regions, wheat exchanged and transported, would this not be a great benefit?
translations.idiomatic: Now wheat has ripened greatly between the Huai and Feng regions; if commuted payments were collected in both places and wheat exchanged and transported, would that not be a great benefit?

sentences.zh: 昔劉晏有轉易之法。

translations.literal: Formerly Liu Yan had a method of exchange and transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan once had a method of exchange and transfer.

sentences.zh: 今歲河北大稔，山東東、兗二郡亦有收。

translations.literal: This year Hebei had a great harvest; Shandong's eastern and Yanzhou commanderies also had yield.
translations.idiomatic: This year Hebei had a great harvest; Shandong's eastern and Yanzhou commanderies also had good yields.

sentences.zh: 誠出內帑二三十萬，分發所司，及時收糴，於國計便。

translations.literal: If truly two or three hundred thousand were drawn from the inner treasury, distributed to the relevant offices, and grain bought in season, it would benefit state finances.
translations.idiomatic: If two or three hundred thousand taels were drawn from the inner treasury, distributed to the relevant offices, and grain bought in season, state finances would benefit.

sentences.zh: 」帝即命議行。

translations.literal: " The emperor at once ordered deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor at once ordered deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 屢遷刑科左給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to left supervising secretary in the Department of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to left supervising secretary in the Department of Justice.

sentences.zh: 十六年秋，出察江防。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixteenth year he went out to inspect Yangzi defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixteenth year he inspected Yangzi defenses.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，福王立，進兵科都給事中，旋擢右僉都御史，巡撫應天、徽州諸府。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year the Prince of Fu was established; he was advanced to chief supervising secretary of the Department of War and soon promoted right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Yingtian, Huizhou, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the next year the Prince of Fu was enthroned; Maodi was made chief supervising secretary of the Department of War and soon right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Yingtian, Huizhou, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時大清兵連破李自成，朝議遣使通好，而難其人。

translations.literal: At the time Great Qing troops had repeatedly defeated Li Zicheng; the court discussed sending envoys to seek peace but found it hard to choose the man.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army had repeatedly defeated Li Zicheng; the court discussed sending envoys to seek peace but could not find the right man.

sentences.zh: 懋第母陳歿於燕，懋第欲因是返柩葬，請行。

translations.literal: Maodi's mother Chen died in Yan; Maodi wished to use this to return the coffin for burial and asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: Maodi's mother Chen had died in the north; he wished to return her coffin for burial and asked to go.

sentences.zh: 乃拜懋第兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，與左都督陳弘範、太仆少卿馬紹愉偕，而令懋第經理河北，聯絡關東諸軍。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Maodi vice minister of war on the right concurrently right vice censor-in-chief, together with left commander-in-chief Chen Hongfan and Court of the Imperial Stud vice minister Ma Shaoyu, while ordering Maodi to manage Hebei and link the Guandong armies.
translations.idiomatic: Maodi was appointed vice minister of war on the right and right vice censor-in-chief, to go with Left Commander-in-Chief Chen Hongfan and Court of the Imperial Stud Vice Minister Ma Shaoyu, while also managing Hebei and linking the Guandong armies.

sentences.zh: 馬紹愉者，故兵部郎官也，嘗為陳新甲通款事至義州而還。

translations.literal: Ma Shaoyu was formerly a Ministry of War director; he had once conducted overtures for Chen Xin jia to Yizhou and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shaoyu was formerly a director in the Ministry of War; he had once conducted peace overtures for Chen Xin jia to Yizhou and returned.

sentences.zh: 新甲既誅，紹愉以督戰致衄，為懋第劾罷。

translations.literal: After Xin jia was executed, Shaoyu for supervising battle suffered defeat and was impeached and dismissed by Maodi.
translations.idiomatic: After Xin jia was executed, Shaoyu was dismissed by Maodi for defeat while supervising battle.

sentences.zh: 及是紹愉已起官郎中，乃進為少卿，副懋第。

translations.literal: By this time Shaoyu had been recalled as director and was advanced to vice minister, assisting Maodi.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shaoyu had been recalled as director and promoted to vice minister to assist Maodi.

sentences.zh: 懋第言：「臣此行致祭先帝後梓宮，訪東宮二王蹤跡。

translations.literal: Maodi said: "On this mission your subject will offer sacrifice at the late emperor's coffin palace and seek traces of the Eastern Palace's two princes.
translations.idiomatic: Maodi said: "On this mission I will offer sacrifice at the late emperor's coffin and seek traces of the crown prince and his brother.

sentences.zh: 臣既充使臣，勢不能兼理封疆。

translations.literal: Your subject being fully an envoy, circumstances do not allow also managing the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: As envoy I cannot also manage the frontier.

sentences.zh: 且紹愉臣所劾罷，不當復與臣共事。

translations.literal: Moreover Shaoyu was dismissed by your subject's impeachment and ought not again serve with your subject.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Shaoyu was dismissed at my impeachment and ought not serve with me again.

sentences.zh: 必用臣經理，則乞命弘範同紹愉出使，而假臣一旅，偕山東撫臣收拾山東以待，不敢復言北行。

translations.literal: If your subject must manage affairs, then I beg that Hongfan go with Shaoyu as envoy while your subject is lent one brigade, together with the Shandong grand coordinator to settle Shandong and wait—I dare not again speak of going north.
translations.idiomatic: If I must manage affairs, then let Hongfan go north with Shaoyu as envoy while I am lent one brigade, together with the Shandong grand coordinator, to settle Shandong—I will not speak of going north.

sentences.zh: 如用臣與弘範北行，則去臣經理，但銜命而往，而罷紹愉勿遣。

translations.literal: If your subject and Hongfan go north, then remove your subject's management duties—only carry the commission and go—and dismiss Shaoyu, do not send him.
translations.idiomatic: If Hongfan and I go north, remove my management duties—I will go only as envoy—and do not send Shaoyu.

sentences.zh: 」閣部議止紹愉，改命原任薊督王永吉。

translations.literal: " The Grand Secretariat deliberated to stop Shaoyu and changed the appointment to former Jizhou governor Wang Yongji.
translations.idiomatic: " The Grand Secretariat agreed to withhold Shaoyu and appointed former Jizhou Governor Wang Yongji instead.

sentences.zh: 王令仍遵前諭。

translations.literal: Wang ordered that the previous instructions still be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang ordered that the previous instructions still be followed.

sentences.zh: 懋第瀕行言：「臣此行，生死未卜。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure Maodi said: "On this mission your subject's life or death cannot be foretold.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing Maodi said: "On this mission I may not return alive.

sentences.zh: 請以辭闕之身，效一言。

translations.literal: I beg, with a body that takes leave of the court, to offer one word.
translations.idiomatic: Allow me, as one who leaves the court, to offer one word.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以先帝仇恥為心，瞻高皇之弓劍，則思成祖列聖之陵寢何存；

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to take the late emperor's enmity and shame to heart; when you gaze upon the High Emperor's bow and sword, then think where the tombs of Chengzu and the successive sage emperors now stand;
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty keep the late emperor's vengeance and shame in your heart; when you look upon the founding emperor's bow and sword, remember what has become of the tombs of the Yongle Emperor and his successors;

sentences.zh: 撫江上之殘黎，則念河北、山東之赤子誰恤。

translations.literal: when you comfort the remnant people along the river, then think who pities the common folk of Hebei and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: when you comfort the remnant people south of the river, remember who cares for the people of Hebei and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 更望時時整頓士馬，必能渡河而戰，始能扼河而守；

translations.literal: I further hope you will constantly drill troops and horses—only if you can cross the river to fight can you then hold the river to defend;
translations.idiomatic: I further hope you will constantly drill your forces—only if you can cross the river to fight can you hold the river to defend;

sentences.zh: 必能扼河而守，始能畫江而安。

translations.literal: only if you can hold the river to defend can you then draw the river as boundary and be secure.
translations.idiomatic: only if you can hold the river can you make the Yangzi your boundary and be secure.

sentences.zh: 」眾韙其言。

translations.literal: " All praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: " All praised his words.

sentences.zh: 王令賫白金十萬兩、幣帛數萬匹，以兵三千人護行。

translations.literal: Wang ordered one hundred thousand taels of white silver and tens of thousands of rolls of silks and cloth presented, with three thousand troops to escort the mission.
translations.idiomatic: Wang ordered one hundred thousand taels of silver and tens of thousands of rolls of silk presented, with three thousand troops as escort.

sentences.zh: 八月，舟渡淮。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they crossed the Huai by boat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month they crossed the Huai by boat.

sentences.zh: 十月朔，次張家灣，本朝傳令止許百人從行。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month they halted at Zhangjiawan; the present dynasty transmitted orders permitting only one hundred men to accompany them.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the tenth month they halted at Zhangjiawan; the Qing court ordered that only one hundred men might accompany them.

sentences.zh: 懋第衰糸至入都門，至則館之鴻臚寺。

translations.literal: Maodi in mourning hemp reached and entered the capital gate; on arrival they lodged him at the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Maodi in mourning dress entered the capital; on arrival he was lodged at the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 請祭告諸陵及改葬先帝，不可，則陳太牢於旅所，哭而奠之。

translations.literal: He asked to offer sacrifice at the imperial tombs and rebury the late emperor; this was not permitted, so he set out the great offering at his lodging, wept, and made offering.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to sacrifice at the imperial tombs and rebury the late emperor; when refused, he set out the great offering at his lodging, wept, and made obeisance.

sentences.zh: 即以是月二十有八日遣還出都。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of that month he was sent back out of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth day of that month he was sent out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 弘範乃請身赴江南招諸將劉澤清等降附，而留懋第等勿遣。

translations.literal: Hongfan then asked to go in person to the south to recruit generals Liu Zeqing and others to surrender, while retaining Maodi and others and not sending them away.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan then asked to go south in person to recruit generals such as Liu Zeqing to surrender, while detaining Maodi and his party.

sentences.zh: 於是自滄州追還懋第，改館太醫院。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Cangzhou they recalled Maodi and changed his lodging to the Imperial Medical Academy.
translations.idiomatic: They then recalled Maodi from Cangzhou and moved him to the Imperial Medical Academy.

sentences.zh: 順治二年六月，聞南京失守，慟哭。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Shunzhi, hearing that Nanjing had fallen, he wept in anguish.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Shunzhi, hearing that Nanjing had fallen, he wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 其從弟懋泰先為吏部員外郎，降賊，後歸本朝授官矣，來謁懋第。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Maotai had first been a Department of Personnel vice director, surrendered to the bandits, later submitted to the present dynasty and received office, and came to visit Maodi.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Maotai had been a vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, surrendered to the rebels, later submitted to the Qing and received office, and came to visit Maodi.

sentences.zh: 懋第曰：「此非吾弟也。

translations.literal: Maodi said: "This is not my brother.
translations.idiomatic: Maodi said: "This is not my brother.

sentences.zh: 」叱出之。

translations.literal: " He shouted and drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: " He shouted and drove him out.

sentences.zh: 至閏月十二日，與從行兵部司務陳用極，遊擊王一斌，都司張良佐、劉統、王廷佐俱以不降誅，而紹愉獲免。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the intercalary month, together with the accompanying Ministry of War clerk Chen Yongji, guerrilla officer Wang Yibin, and regional commanders Zhang Liangzuo, Liu Tong, and Wang Tingzuo—all were executed for not surrendering—while Shaoyu was spared.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day of the intercalary month, Ministry of War clerk Chen Yongji, guerrilla officer Wang Yibin, and regional commanders Zhang Liangzuo, Liu Tong, and Wang Tingzuo were all executed for refusing to surrender; Shaoyu alone was spared.

sentences.zh: 祁彪佳，字弘吉，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Qi Biaojia, styled Hongji, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Biaojia, courtesy name Hongji, was from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 祖父世清白吏。

translations.literal: His grandfather's family for generations were upright officials.
translations.idiomatic: His family for generations had been upright officials.

sentences.zh: 彪佳生而英特，豐姿絕人。

translations.literal: Biaojia from birth was outstanding in talent, with bearing surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: Biaojia was gifted from birth and striking in appearance.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，第天啟二年進士，授興化府推官。

translations.literal: At his capping he placed in the civil service examination in the second year of Tianqi and was appointed judicial assistant in Xinghua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he received his jinshi degree in the second year of Tianqi and was appointed judicial assistant in Xinghua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始至，吏民易其年少。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, clerks and people took him lightly for his youth.
translations.idiomatic: When he first arrived, officials and commoners underestimated him for his youth.

sentences.zh: 及治事，剖決精明，皆大畏服。

translations.literal: When he handled affairs, his judgments were keen and precise, and all greatly feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took up cases, his judgments were sharp and precise, and all came to respect him.

sentences.zh: 外艱歸。

translations.literal: On his father's death he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，起御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was recalled as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was recalled as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 疏陳賞罰之要，言：「黔功因一級疑，稽三年之敘，且恩及督撫總帥帷幄大臣，而陷敵沖鋒之士不預，何以勵行間。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the essentials of rewards and punishments, saying: "Qian merit because of one grade's doubt was delayed three years in promotion, and grace reached grand coordinators, commanders-in-chief, and grand secretaries in the tent, while those who fell into the enemy and charged in the van were not included—how can one encourage those in the ranks?
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on rewards and punishments: "Merit in Guizhou was held up over a single grade, promotion delayed three years, while grand coordinators, commanders, and grand secretaries were rewarded—yet men who charged the enemy were left out. How can the ranks be encouraged?

sentences.zh: 山東之變，六誠連陷，未嘗議及一官，欺蒙之習不可不破。

translations.literal: In the Shandong disaster six walled cities fell in succession, yet not one official was discussed—habits of deception cannot go unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shandong disaster six cities fell in succession without a single official held accountable—the habit of deception must be broken.

sentences.zh: 」帝即命議行。

translations.literal: " The emperor at once ordered deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor at once ordered deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 又言：「九列之長，詰責時聞，四朝遺老或蒙重譴。

translations.literal: He also said: "Heads of the nine ministries are rebuked from time to time; survivors of four reigns sometimes receive heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Heads of the nine ministries are rebuked from time to time; survivors of four reigns sometimes receive heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 諸臣怵嚴威，競迎合以保名位。

translations.literal: Officials fear stern authority and compete in flattery to preserve name and position.
translations.idiomatic: Officials fear stern authority and compete to flatter and preserve their positions.

sentences.zh: 臣所慮於大臣者此也。

translations.literal: What your subject fears regarding great ministers is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I fear regarding great ministers.

sentences.zh: 方伯或一二考，臺員或十余載，竟不得遷除，監司守令多貶秩停俸。

translations.literal: Regional governors may serve one or two reviews, censorate members ten years or more, yet in the end receive no transfer or promotion; surveillance commissioners, prefects, and magistrates are mostly demoted in rank and salaries suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Regional governors may serve one or two reviews, censorate members ten years or more, yet receive no promotion; surveillance commissioners, prefects, and magistrates are often demoted and salaries suspended.

sentences.zh: 臣子精神才具無余地，展布曷由。

translations.literal: Ministers' spirit and talent have no room left—how can they deploy themselves?
translations.idiomatic: Officials have no room left to deploy their talents—how can they serve effectively?

sentences.zh: 急功赴名之民不勝其掩罪匿瑕。

translations.literal: People eager for quick achievement and reputation cannot bear their concealing crimes and hiding flaws.
translations.idiomatic: Men eager for quick success cannot bear scrutiny of their concealed faults.

sentences.zh: 臣所慮於小臣者此也。

translations.literal: What your subject fears regarding lesser officials is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I fear regarding lesser officials.

sentences.zh: 國家聞鼙鼓思將帥，茍得其人，推轂築壇，禮亦宜之。

translations.literal: When the state hears war drums it thinks of generals; if the right man is found, pushing the chariot wheel and building the altar—the ritual is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: When war drums sound the state thinks of generals; if the right man is found, to push the chariot wheel and build the altar is fitting ritual.

sentences.zh: 若必依序循資，冒濫之竇雖可清，獎拔之術或未盡。

translations.literal: If one must follow order and seniority, the channel of reckless promotion may be cleared, yet the art of rewarding and elevating may not be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: If promotion must follow seniority alone, reckless advancement may be curbed, but the art of rewarding merit may be incomplete.

sentences.zh: 臣所慮於武臣者此也。

translations.literal: What your subject fears regarding military officers is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I fear regarding military officers.

sentences.zh: 撫按則使中官監視會同，隙開水火，其忠顯；

translations.literal: Grand coordinators are made to have eunuchs observe and join them—gaps open like fire and water, and loyalty is displayed;
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinators are made to work with supervising eunuchs—gaps open like fire and water, and loyalty is displayed;

sentences.zh: 潛通交結，其患深。

translations.literal: secret communication and collusion—the harm is deep.
translations.idiomatic: secret collusion—the harm runs deep.

sentences.zh: 臣所慮於內臣者此也。

translations.literal: What your subject fears regarding inner courtiers is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I fear regarding inner courtiers.

sentences.zh: 」忤旨譙責。

translations.literal: " He offended the imperial will and was rebuked and blamed.
translations.idiomatic: " He offended the throne and was rebuked.

sentences.zh: 尋上《合籌天下全局疏》，以策關、寧，制登海為二大要。

translations.literal: Soon he submitted "Memorial on Coordinating the Overall Situation of the Realm," taking policy toward the passes and Ningxia and controlling Deng and Hai as two great essentials.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted "Memorial on Coordinating the Overall Situation of the Realm," making policy toward the frontier passes and Ningxia and control of Dengzhou and Haizhou the two great priorities.

sentences.zh: 分析中州、秦、晉之流賊，江右、楚、粵之山賊，浙、閩、東粵之海賊，滇、黔、楚、蜀之土賊為四大勢。

translations.literal: He analyzed roving bandits of the central plains, Qin, and Jin; mountain bandits of Jiangxi, Chu, and Guangdong; sea bandits of Zhe, Fujian, and eastern Guangdong; and native bandits of Yunnan, Guizhou, Chu, and Shu as four great forces.
translations.idiomatic: He analyzed roving bandits in the central plains, Qin, and Shanxi; mountain bandits in Jiangxi, Huguang, and Guangdong; sea bandits in Zhejiang, Fujian, and eastern Guangdong; and native chieftain rebels in Yunnan, Guizhou, Huguang, and Sichuan as four great threats.

sentences.zh: 極控制駕馭之宜，而歸其要於戢行伍以節餉，實衛所以銷兵。

translations.literal: He exhaustively set forth what was fitting in control and mastery, returning the essentials to restraining ranks to save rations—solid defense is how arms are dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: He set out in detail how to control them, concluding that the key was to restrain the ranks and save pay—solid defense is how arms are laid down.

sentences.zh: 復陳民間十四大苦：曰裏甲，曰虛糧，曰行戶，曰搜贓，曰欽提，曰隔提，曰訐訟，曰窩訪，曰私稅，曰私鑄，曰解運，曰馬戶，曰鹽丁，曰難民。

translations.literal: He further set forth the people's fourteen great sufferings: the lijia system, false grain accounts, broker households, search for booty, imperial extradition, indirect extradition, malicious litigation, secret investigations, private taxes, private coining, transport conscription, horse households, salt laborers, and refugees.
translations.idiomatic: He listed fourteen great popular grievances: the lijia system, false grain accounts, broker households, searches for booty, imperial extradition, indirect extradition, malicious litigation, secret investigations, private taxes, private coining, transport conscription, horse households, salt laborers, and refugees.

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，下之所司。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and sent them down to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his words and referred them to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 出按蘇、松諸府，廉積猾四人杖殺之。

translations.literal: Going out to inspect Suzhou, Songjiang, and other prefectures, he found four long-accumulated rascals and had them beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: On inspection tour in Suzhou, Songjiang, and other prefectures, he found four long-standing rascals and had them beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 宜興民發首輔周延儒祖墓，又焚翰林陳於鼎、於泰廬，亦發其祖墓。

translations.literal: People of Yixing opened Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru's ancestral tomb; they also burned the lodges of Hanlin members Chen Yuding and Chen Yutai and opened their ancestral tombs as well.
translations.idiomatic: People of Yixing opened Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru's ancestral tomb; they also burned the lodges of Hanlin members Chen Yuding and Chen Yutai and opened their ancestral tombs.

sentences.zh: 彪佳捕治如法，而於延儒無所徇，延儒憾之。

translations.literal: Biaojia arrested and punished according to law, showing no favor to Yanru; Yanru resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Biaojia arrested and punished them according to law, showing no favor to Yanru, who resented it.

sentences.zh: 回道考核，降俸，尋以侍養歸。

translations.literal: On return from tour he was reviewed and his salary reduced; soon he returned home to attend his parents.
translations.idiomatic: On return from tour his salary was reduced; he soon went home to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 家居九年，母服終，召掌河南道事。

translations.literal: He lived at home nine years; when his mother's mourning ended he was summoned to head Henan circuit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home nine years; when his mother's mourning ended he was summoned to head Henan circuit affairs.

sentences.zh: 十六年佐大計，問遺莫敢及門。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he assisted the great review; gifts no one dared bring to his door.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he assisted the great capital review; no one dared offer him gifts.

sentences.zh: 刷卷南畿，乞休，不允，便道還家。

translations.literal: Reviewing files in the southern capital region, he asked to retire; this was not granted, and he returned home by convenient route.
translations.idiomatic: While reviewing files in the southern capital region he asked to retire; when refused, he returned home by a convenient route.

sentences.zh: 北都變聞，謁福王於南京。

translations.literal: Hearing of the northern capital's calamity, he paid respects to the Prince of Fu at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the fall of the northern capital, he paid his respects to the Prince of Fu at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 王監國，或請登極。

translations.literal: When the prince supervised the state, some asked that he ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince supervised the state, some urged him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 彪佳請發喪，服滿議其儀，從之。

translations.literal: Biaojia asked to issue mourning; when the mourning period ended they discussed the rites, and this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Biaojia asked that mourning be proclaimed; when the mourning period ended they discussed the rites, and his proposal was followed.

sentences.zh: 高傑兵擾揚州，民奔避江南，奸民乘機剽兌攵，命彪佳往宣諭，斬倡亂者數人，一方遂安。

translations.literal: Gao Jie's troops disturbed Yangzhou; people fled south of the river; wicked people seized the chance to plunder; Biaojia was ordered to go proclaim and instruct, beheaded several ringleaders, and the region was then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jie's troops disturbed Yangzhou and people fled south of the river; ruffians seized the chance to plunder; Biaojia was sent to proclaim the court's will, beheaded several ringleaders, and the region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 遷大理寺丞，旋擢右僉都御史，巡撫江南。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and soon promoted right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and soon right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 蘇州諸生檄討其鄉官從賊者，奸民和之。

translations.literal: Suzhou students issued a manifesto to denounce local officials who followed the bandits; wicked people joined them.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou students issued a manifesto denouncing local officials who had served the rebels; ruffians joined in.

sentences.zh: 少詹事項煜及大理寺正錢位坤、通政司參議宋學顯、禮部員外郎湯有慶之家皆被焚劫。

translations.literal: Junior mentor Xiang Yu and Court of Judicial Review director Qian Weikun, Office of Transmission vice commissioner Song Xuexian, and Ministry of Rites vice director Tang Youqing—all their homes were burned and looted.
translations.idiomatic: The homes of Junior Mentor Xiang Yu, Director Qian Weikun of the Court of Judicial Review, Vice Commissioner Song Xuexian of the Office of Transmission, and Vice Director Tang Youqing of the Ministry of Rites were all burned and looted.

sentences.zh: 常熟又焚給事中時敏家，毀其三代四棺。

translations.literal: In Changshu they also burned supervising secretary Shi Min's home and destroyed four coffins of three generations.
translations.idiomatic: In Changshu they also burned Supervising Secretary Shi Min's home and destroyed four coffins spanning three generations.

sentences.zh: 彪佳請議從逆諸臣罪，而治焚掠之徒以加等，從之。

translations.literal: Biaojia asked to deliberate the crimes of officials who followed the rebels and to punish arson and looting with aggravated sentences; this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Biaojia asked that the crimes of officials who had served the rebels be deliberated and that arson and looting be punished with aggravated sentences; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔設廠衛緝事官。

translations.literal: An edict ordered establishment of investigation officers in the factory guards.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the establishment of secret police in the factory guards.

sentences.zh: 彪佳上言：「洪武初，官民有犯，或收系錦衣衛，高皇帝見非法淩虐，焚其刑具，送囚刑部。

translations.literal: Biaojia memorialized: "In the beginning of Hongwu, when officials or people offended, some were detained in the Embroidered Uniform Guard; the High Emperor saw illegal abuse, burned their instruments of torture, and sent prisoners to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Biaojia wrote: "Early in Hongwu, when officials or commoners offended, some were detained in the Embroidered Uniform Guard; the founding emperor saw illegal abuse, burned their torture implements, and sent prisoners to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 是祖制原無詔獄也。

translations.literal: Thus by ancestral institution there originally were no imperial prisons.
translations.idiomatic: By ancestral institution there were originally no imperial prisons.

sentences.zh: 後乃以羅織為事，雖曰朝廷爪牙，實為權奸鷹狗。

translations.literal: Later they made frame-ups their business; though called the court's claws and teeth, in truth they were powerful traitors' hawks and hounds.
translations.idiomatic: Later they made frame-ups their trade; though called the court's agents, they were in truth the henchmen of powerful traitors.

sentences.zh: 舉朝盡知其枉，而法司無敢雪。

translations.literal: The whole court knew they were wronged, yet the judiciary dared not clear them.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court knew the victims were innocent, yet the judiciary dared not clear them.

sentences.zh: 慘酷等來、周，平反無徐、杜。

translations.literal: Cruelty matched Lai and Zhou; reversal of wrongful verdicts had no Xu or Du.
translations.idiomatic: Cruelty matched the torturers Lai Jun and Zhou Xing; there was no Xu Jie or Du Jin to reverse wrongful verdicts.

sentences.zh: 此詔獄之弊也。

translations.literal: These are the abuses of imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: These are the abuses of the imperial prison system.

sentences.zh: 洪武十五年改儀鑾司為錦衣衛，專掌直駕侍衛等事，未嘗令緝事也。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongwu the Ceremonial Guard Office was changed to the Embroidered Uniform Guard, solely managing imperial escort and guard duties, never ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Hongwu the Ceremonial Guard Office became the Embroidered Uniform Guard, charged only with imperial escort and guard duties, never with investigation.

sentences.zh: 永樂間設立東廠，始開告密門。

translations.literal: In the Yongle period the Eastern Depot was established, first opening the door to secret denunciation.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongle reign the Eastern Depot was established, opening the door to secret denunciation.

sentences.zh: 兇人投為廝役，赤手鉅萬。

translations.literal: Vicious men entered as attendants and with empty hands gained tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Vicious men entered service as attendants and with empty hands amassed fortunes.

sentences.zh: 飛誣及於善良，招承出於私拷，怨憤滿乎京畿。

translations.literal: Flying accusations reached the good; confessions came from private torture; resentment filled the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: False accusations reached the innocent; confessions were extracted by private torture; resentment filled the capital region.

sentences.zh: 欲絕苞苴，而苞苴彌盛；

translations.literal: Wishing to end bribery, bribery grew all the more;
translations.idiomatic: They wished to end bribery, yet bribery grew worse;

sentences.zh: 欲清奸宄，而奸宄益多。

translations.literal: wishing to clear treachery, treachery increased yet more.
translations.idiomatic: they wished to clear out wrongdoing, yet wrongdoing multiplied.

sentences.zh: 此緝事之弊也。

translations.literal: These are the abuses of secret investigation.
translations.idiomatic: These are the abuses of secret investigation.

sentences.zh: 古者刑不上大夫。

translations.literal: In antiquity punishment did not reach great officers.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity punishment did not reach great officers.

sentences.zh: 逆瑾用事，始去衣受杖。

translations.literal: When the traitor Jin held power, they first stripped robes for beating.
translations.idiomatic: When the traitor Liu Jin held power, officials were first stripped and beaten at court.

sentences.zh: 本無可殺之罪，乃蒙必死之刑。

translations.literal: Originally there was no crime warranting death, yet they received sentences of certain death.
translations.idiomatic: Men guilty of no capital crime received sentences of certain death.

sentences.zh: 朝廷受愎諫之名，天下反歸忠直之譽。

translations.literal: The court received a name for obstinate rejection of remonstrance, while the realm instead gave reputation for loyalty and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: The court gained a reputation for obstinacy, while the realm gave the victims a reputation for loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 此廷杖之弊也。

translations.literal: These are the abuses of court beating.
translations.idiomatic: These are the abuses of court corporal punishment.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，乃命五城御史體訪，而緝事官不設。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, they ordered the Five Cities investigating censors to conduct inquiries in person, and investigation officers were not established.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, the court ordered the Five Cities investigating censors to conduct inquiries in person, and secret police were not established.

sentences.zh: 督輔部將劉肇基、陳可立、張應夢、於永綬駐京口，浙江入衛都司黃之奎亦部水陸兵三四千戍其地。

translations.literal: Supervisory auxiliary generals Liu Zhaoji, Chen Keli, Zhang Yingmeng, and Yu Yongshou were stationed at Jingkou; Zhejiang capital-guard regional commander Huang Zhikui also deployed three or four thousand land and water troops to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: Auxiliary generals Liu Zhaoji, Chen Keli, Zhang Yingmeng, and Yu Yongshou were stationed at Jingkou; Zhejiang Capital Guard Regional Commander Huang Zhikui also deployed three or four thousand land and water troops to garrison the area.

sentences.zh: 之奎禦軍嚴。

translations.literal: Zhikui governed the army strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhikui disciplined his troops strictly.

sentences.zh: 四將兵恣橫，刃傷民，浙兵縛而投之江，遂有隙。

translations.literal: The four generals' troops were wanton; blades wounded the people; Zhe troops bound them and threw them in the river—thus a rift opened.
translations.idiomatic: The four generals' troops were unruly and wounded civilians; Zhejiang troops bound them and threw them in the river, opening a rift between the armies.

sentences.zh: 已而守備李大開統浙兵斫鎮兵馬，鎮兵與相擊，射殺大開。

translations.literal: Before long garrison commander Li Dakai led Zhe troops to hack at the garrison troops' horses; garrison troops fought back and shot Li Dakai dead.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Garrison Commander Li Dakai led Zhejiang troops to attack the garrison forces' horses; the garrison troops fought back and shot Li Dakai dead.

sentences.zh: 亂兵大焚掠，死者四百人。

translations.literal: Mutinous troops burned and looted greatly; four hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: Mutinous troops burned and looted on a large scale; four hundred people died.

sentences.zh: 彪佳至，永綬等遁去。

translations.literal: When Biaojia arrived, Yongshou and the others fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Biaojia arrived, Yongshou and the others fled.

sentences.zh: 彪佳劾治四將罪，赒恤被難家，民大悅。

translations.literal: Biaojia impeached and punished the four generals, compensated families that suffered, and the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Biaojia impeached and punished the four generals, compensated the victims' families, and the people were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 高傑駐瓜洲，跋扈甚，彪佳克期往會。

translations.literal: Gao Jie was stationed at Guazhou, very overbearing; Biaojia set a date to go meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jie was stationed at Guazhou and was very overbearing; Biaojia set a date to meet him.

sentences.zh: 至期，風大作，傑意彪佳必無來。

translations.literal: When the day came, wind blew fiercely; Jie thought Biaojia would surely not come.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came a great wind blew; Jie assumed Biaojia would not come.

sentences.zh: 彪佳攜數卒沖風渡，傑大駭異，盡撤兵衛，會彪佳於大觀樓。

translations.literal: Biaojia took several soldiers and crossed against the wind; Jie was greatly startled, fully withdrew military guards, and met Biaojia at the Daguan Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Biaojia took a few soldiers and crossed against the wind; Jie was astonished, dismissed all his guards, and met Biaojia at the Daguan Tower.

sentences.zh: 彪佳披肝膈，勉以忠義，共獎王室。

translations.literal: Biaojia laid open his heart, exhorted him with loyalty and righteousness, and together encouraged the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Biaojia spoke from the heart, exhorted him to loyalty and righteousness, and together they pledged service to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 傑感嘆曰：「傑閱人多矣，如公，傑甘為死！

translations.literal: Jie sighed in emotion: "Jie has seen many men; for one like you, sir, Jie would gladly die!
translations.idiomatic: Jie exclaimed: "I have seen many men; for one like you, sir, I would gladly die!

sentences.zh: 公一日在吳，傑一日遵公約矣。

translations.literal: While you are one day in Wu, Jie will one day keep your agreement."
translations.idiomatic: As long as you remain in Wu, I will keep your agreement for one day more."

sentences.zh: 」共飯而別。

translations.literal: " They shared a meal and parted.
translations.idiomatic: " They shared a meal and parted.

sentences.zh: 群小疾彪佳，競詆諆，以沮登極、立潞王為言，彪佳竟移疾去。

translations.literal: Petty men resented Biaojia and competed in slander, speaking of obstructing enthronement and establishing the Prince of Lu; Biaojia in the end cited illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men resented Biaojia and competed in slander, accusing him of obstructing enthronement and favoring the Prince of Lu; Biaojia finally pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，南都失守。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year the Southern Capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the next year the Southern Capital fell.

sentences.zh: 六月，杭州繼失，彪佳即絕粒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Hangzhou fell in turn; Biaojia at once stopped eating grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Hangzhou fell in turn; Biaojia at once stopped eating.

sentences.zh: 至閏月四日，紿家人先寢，端坐池中而死，年四十有四。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the intercalary month he deceived his family into sleeping first, sat upright in a pool, and died, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the intercalary month he sent his family to bed first, sat upright in a pool, and died at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 唐王贈少保、兵部尚書，謚忠敏。

translations.literal: The Prince of Tang posthumously granted him Junior Guardian and Minister of War, with posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tang posthumously made him Junior Guardian and Minister of War, with the posthumous title Loyal and Keen.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：張慎言、徐石麒等皆北都舊臣，剛方練達，所建白悉有裨時政。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Zhang Shenyan, Xu Shiqi, and the rest were all old ministers of the northern capital, upright, stern, and practiced; what they proposed all benefited current policy.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Zhang Shenyan, Xu Shiqi, and the rest were old ministers of the northern capital—upright, stern, and practiced—and their proposals all benefited state affairs.

sentences.zh: 令其受事熙朝，從容展布，庶幾乎列卿之良也。

translations.literal: Had they received office in a flourishing age and deployed themselves at ease, they might nearly have been fine among the ranked ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Had they served in a flourishing age and been able to act at ease, they might have ranked among the finest ministers.

sentences.zh: 而遭時不造，內外交訌，動輒齟齬，雖老成何能設施幹濟哉！

translations.literal: But encountering an ill-fated time, with strife within and without, at every turn friction—though seasoned in years, how could they carry out practical achievement!
translations.idiomatic: But they met an ill-fated age of strife within and without, friction at every turn—even seasoned statesmen could not achieve practical results!

sentences.zh: 左懋第仗節全貞，蹈死不悔，於奉使之義，亦無愧焉。

translations.literal: Zuo Maodi upheld his commission and preserved integrity whole, treading death without regret—in the duty of bearing an embassy, he too was without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Maodi upheld his commission and preserved his integrity, facing death without regret—in the duty of an envoy he too was without shame.
